example_en3: Strictly speaking, Chinese consists of hundreds of dialects.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To swaddle 勹 a baby 巳; 勹 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 包括: Placed before nouns to indicate inclusion in a previously mentioned category.
example_zh3: 风俗习惯包括食物，庆祝和舞蹈。
example_en3: Customs include food, celebrations and dancing.

grammar_note: 薄: Placed before nouns to describe thinness or flimsiness.
example_en1: A woman is ever fickle and changeable.
example_en2: Cut the meat into thin slices.
example_en3: The air is thin at the summit.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': "Jade 玉 kept in one's house 宀"}
grammar_note: 宝贝: Used as a noun to express endearment for loved ones or cherished items.
example_en3: He is the baby of the family.

grammar_note: 保持: Placed as a main verb to indicate maintaining or keeping something.
保存: Placed as a verb to indicate preserving or keeping something.
example_en1: Keep it in a cool place.
example_en3: He requested me to keep it secret.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': "Jade 玉 kept in one's house 宀"}
grammar_note: 宝贵: Placed after nouns to describe them as valuable or precious.
example_en2: Time is more precious than anything else.
example_zh3: 时间是世界上最宝贵的东西。
example_en3: Time is the most precious thing in the world.

Translation: continue to have; persist; to retain; hold back
grammar_note: 保留: Placed as a verb to indicate keeping or preserving something.
example_en3: Leave the room as it is.

grammar_note: 保险: Serves as a noun indicating guarantee or insurance in a sentence.
example_zh2: 为什么你买了旅行保险？
example_en2: Why did you buy travel insurance?
example_zh3: 保险箱的钥匙在我这儿。
example_en3: I have the key to the safe.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 扌 cuffing 又 a criminal 卩, representing sentencing'}
grammar_note: 报道: Placed after subject to indicate reporting action.
example_zh1: 他觉得必须报道这件事。
example_en1: He felt compelled to report the incident.
example_zh2: 汤姆写了篇非常有深度的报道。
example_en2: Tom wrote a very profound report.
example_zh3: 关于这个问题，我觉得垃圾媒体只报道了很片面的信息。
example_en3: Concerning this issue, I feel that the trash media only report biased information.

Translation: report for duty; check in; register
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 扌 cuffing 又 a criminal 卩, representing sentencing'}
grammar_note: 报到: 动词，表示办理注册或报道手续。
example_zh2: 今天早上我九点去学校报到了。
example_en2: This morning, I reported to school at nine o'clock.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 扌 cuffing 又 a criminal 卩, representing sentencing'}
grammar_note: 报告: Used as a noun for a report or can be a verb to inform someone.
example_en2: I am writing my internship report.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 扌 cuffing 又 a criminal 卩, representing sentencing'}
grammar_note: 报社: Serves as a noun representing a newspaper office in sentences.
example_zh1: 我为这家报社工作四年了。
example_en1: I have been working for this newspaper for 4 years.
example_zh2: 这家报社在当地知名度颇高。
example_en2: This newspaper is well known in the local area.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': "To wrap 包 in one's arms 扌; 包 also provides the pronunciation"}
grammar_note: 抱怨: Placed as a verb to express complaint or dissatisfaction.
悲观: Used as an adjective to describe a pessimistic outlook.
example_en3: I am by turns an optimist and a pessimist.

grammar_note: 背: 动词，意为“背着”或表示记忆、方向等。
背景: A noun placed after descriptors to indicate contextual background.
example_zh2: 图片的背景是一座城堡。
example_en2: There is a castle in the background of the picture.
example_zh3: 如果你不明白一件事，那是因为你没有意识到它的背景。
example_en3: If you don't understand something, it's because you aren't aware of its context.

grammar_note: 被子: A noun representing a quilt, used as an object in sentences.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A tree 木 with its roots highlighted'}
grammar_note: 本科: Indicates the field of undergraduate study in a sentence.
example_zh1: 本科是很多学生的第一选择。
example_en1: Many students choose undergraduate courses as their first choice.
example_en2: I study Chinese in my undergraduate program.
example_zh3: 他的本科专业是计算机科学。
example_en3: His undergraduate major is computer science.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A tree 木 with its roots highlighted'}
grammar_note: 本领: Placed as a noun to express one's capability or skill in a specific area.
example_en2: He has a very strong capability.
example_zh3: 小猫学会了爬树的本领。
example_en3: The little cat learned the ability to climb trees.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A tree 木 with its roots highlighted'}
grammar_note: 本质: Placed after descriptors to refer to the intrinsic nature of something.
example_en1: That is the essence of the matter.
example_en2: The essence of liberty is mathematics.
example_zh3: 喏，这是我的秘密。很简单。只有用心才能看到本质的东西。精髓是眼睛看不见的。
example_en3: And now here is my secret, a very simple secret: It is only with the heart that one can see rightly; what is essential is invisible to the eye.

Translation: each other; both parties; one another
grammar_note: 彼此: Placed between nouns or verbs to indicate mutual action.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Two spoons 匕 side-by-side; 匕 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 比例: Placed after nouns to indicate scale or ratio between them.
example_zh1: 1772 年，埃斯皮利先生計算出法國人口超過 2,200 萬人；其中男性 10,562,631 人，女性 11,451,726 人；因此，女性與男性的比例約為 14 比 13。
example_en1: Monsieur D'Espilly, in the year 1772, calculated the population of France at upwards of 22 millions; namely, 10,562,631 males, and 11,451,726 females; consequently the proportion of females to males was about 14 to 13.

Translation: after all; all in all; when all is said and done
grammar_note: 毕竟: Placed at the beginning or middle of a sentence to concede a point.
example_zh2: 他毕竟是那个时代的人。
example_en2: He's a product of his time.
example_zh3: 毕竟，我应认真相信些什么？
example_en3: In the end, what must I really believe in?

Translation: to avoid; refrain from; prevent something from happening
grammar_note: 避免: Placed at the beginning of a sentence as a verb to indicate avoiding something.
必然: Placed after verbs to indicate inevitability.
example_en1: That he will succeed is certain.

grammar_note: 必要: Placed after verbs to indicate necessity or essentiality.
example_en1: There's no reason to be alarmed.
example_en2: He doesn't have to wash the car.

grammar_note: 编辑: Can function as a verb (to edit/compile) or a noun (editor).
example_en1: You don't want to be an editor?
example_zh2: 我们应该对人使用基因编辑吗？
example_en2: Should we use genetic engineering on people?

grammar_note: 鞭炮: A noun representing firecrackers in a phrase or clause describing celebrations.
example_zh1: 鞭炮在新年时很受欢迎。
example_en1: Firecrackers are very popular during the New Year.
example_zh3: 孩子们喜欢放鞭炮来庆祝节日。
example_en3: Children like to set off firecrackers to celebrate festivals.

Translation: convenience; excrement or urine; relieve oneself
grammar_note: 便: Placed before verbs to indicate convenience or immediately.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bitter 辛 exchange of words 讠'}
grammar_note: 辩论: Used as a verb to indicate engaging in an argument or debate.
example_en2: Bill is skillful in arguing and debating.

grammar_note: 标点: Indicates punctuation used in writing.
example_en1: An exclamation mark is a punctuation mark.
example_zh2: 他们说的话，我连标点符号都不信。
example_en2: I do not trust a single word that comes out of their mouths.

grammar_note: 标志: Can function as a noun indicating a sign or symbol, or as a verb to denote marking.
example_zh1: 自我怀疑是聪明的第一标志。
example_en1: To have doubts about oneself is the first sign of intelligence.
example_zh2: 你可以到有“银联”标志的ATM机里去取钱。
example_en2: You can withdraw money from ATMs that have the "UnionPay" logo.
example_zh3: 我的大学今年正在庆祝建校一百周年，因此你到处都可以看到带有它颜色，标志和吉祥物的横幅。
example_en3: My university is celebrating its centennial this year, so you can see banners with its colors, logo, and mascot all over the place.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Fur 毛 clothing 衣; a shawl or wrap'}
grammar_note: 表达: Placed as a verb to indicate expressing an opinion or idea.
example_zh2: 这种表达方式很中国化。

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Fur 毛 clothing 衣; a shawl or wrap'}
grammar_note: 表面: Placed before nouns to refer to the surface or appearance of something.
example_en1: All that glitters is not gold.
example_zh2: 地球的表面有七成是水。
example_en2: The surface of the earth is 70% water.
example_zh3: 美貌只是表面性的东西。

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Fur 毛 clothing 衣; a shawl or wrap'}
grammar_note: 表明: Placed after verbs to state clearly or indicate something.
example_en1: A DNA test showed he was innocent.
example_zh2: 所有迹象表明她好起来了。
example_en2: All the signs are that she is getting better.
example_zh3: 這表明我們對自身的認知很少。
example_en3: That shows how little we know of ourselves.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Fur 毛 clothing 衣; a shawl or wrap'}
grammar_note: 表情: Placed after a subject to describe facial expression or look.
example_zh1: 你真该看看玛丽脸上的表情。
example_en1: You should have seen the look on Mary's face.
example_zh2: 他说话时，显然带着高兴的表情。
example_zh3: 我从你的表情猜到你有好消息。
example_en3: I perceive by your face that you have good news.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Fur 毛 clothing 衣; a shawl or wrap'}
grammar_note: 表现: Placed after verbs to describe how actions are carried out.
example_en1: I'm not going to show any fear.
example_en2: He behaved as if he were crazy.
example_en3: He behaves as if he were insane.

grammar_note: 冰激凌: A noun referring to ice cream in a sentence.
example_en2: Leave me a bit of ice cream.
example_zh3: 我喜欢吃巧克力味的冰激凌。
example_en3: I like to eat chocolate flavored ice cream.

grammar_note: 病毒: Placed as a noun in sentences to refer to viruses.
example_en2: The virus is starting to mutate.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To sow seeds 番 by hand 扌; 番 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 播放: Placed after subject to indicate broadcasting action.
example_zh3: 我MP3播放器的电池没电了。
example_en3: The battery of my MP3-player was empty.

grammar_note: 玻璃: A noun representing glass as a material or object in sentences.
博物馆: Serves as a noun representing a place for exhibition and preservation of artifacts.
example_en2: Where is the entrance to the museum?
example_en3: Where is the entrance to the museum?

grammar_note: 脖子: A noun representing the neck part of the body.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird flying toward the sky 一'}
grammar_note: 不断: Placed before verbs to indicate continuous action without interruption.
example_zh2: 小脑需要连续不断的血液供给。
example_en2: The cerebellum requires continuous blood supply.
example_zh3: 在过敏的季节不断地擤他的鼻子.
example_en3: Constantly blowing his nose in allergy season.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird flying toward the sky 一'}
grammar_note: 不见得: Placed after a statement to express doubt or negation.
example_en1: What he says is not necessarily true.
example_en2: He is unlikely to come today.
example_zh3: 销售部门和营销部门的目标不见得一样。
example_en3: The objectives of the marketing department and the sales department are not necessarily the same.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird flying toward the sky 一'}
grammar_note: 不耐烦: Used as an adjective to describe being impatient.
example_en1: The longer we waited, the more impatient we became.
example_en2: Dad's in an impatient mood today.
example_zh3: 母亲从来没有因为我们而不耐烦。
example_en3: Mother is never impatient with us.

Translation: not important; not serious It doesn't matter; never mind
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird flying toward the sky 一'}
grammar_note: 不要紧: Used at the end of sentences to express that something is not important or serious.
example_en1: I don't care if it's a bit cold.
example_zh2: 脸色这么差不要紧吗？要不还是去一趟医院比较好吧？
example_en2: Your face looks pale. Are you OK? Maybe it would be better if you went to the hospital, don't you think?

grammar_note: 补充: Placed after verbs to indicate adding or replenishing something.
example_zh1: 我刚才说的内容，你想补充么？
example_en1: Is there anything you want to add to what I just said?
example_zh2: 您对我说的话有什么要补充的吗？
example_en2: Would you like to add anything to what I've said?
example_zh3: 请告诉我，我还有什么需要补充的。
example_en3: Please tell me what else I need to add.

grammar_note: 布: Serves as a noun representing cloth or textile in sentences.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird flying toward the sky 一'}
grammar_note: 不安: Placed after stative verbs to express uneasiness or instability.
example_en2: I've been feeling a little restless.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird flying toward the sky 一'}
grammar_note: 不得了: Placed after an adjective to intensify its meaning, indicating extremity.
example_en3: I don't know whether to cry or to laugh.

grammar_note: 部门: Placed after measure words or used alone as a noun to refer to departments or sections.
example_en1: Who's in charge of the sales section?
example_en2: Who's in charge of this section?

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird flying toward the sky 一'}
grammar_note: 不然: Used at the beginning of a sentence to mean "otherwise" or "if not."

Translation: it would be better to …not as good as
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird flying toward the sky 一'}
grammar_note: 不如: Placed before a comparison to express preference or inferiority.
example_en3: Better to live dishonored than die proud.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Modern form of 歨; putting one foot 止 in front of the other'}
grammar_note: 步骤: Placed after quantifiers to refer to procedures or steps in a process.
example_en2: Making rice involves written steps on paper.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird flying toward the sky 一'}
grammar_note: 不足: Placed after nouns to indicate insufficiency.
example_en2: The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.
example_en3: His proposal is not worth talking about.

grammar_note: 财产: Placed after measure words or as subject/predicate in sentences discussing assets.
example_zh1: Brian 丢下了自己的财产。
example_zh2: 我把我的财产托付给他。
example_en2: I entrusted my property to him.
example_zh3: 他继承了他父亲的财产。
example_en3: He succeeded to his father's property.

Translation: to step on; to stamp on; trample
grammar_note: 踩: Placed after subjects to indicate stepping on or stamping on objects.
example_en3: He stepped on my foot on purpose.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand picking 爫 fruit from a tree 木'}
grammar_note: 采访: Used as a verb to indicate conducting an interview.
彩虹: A noun representing a rainbow in a sentence.
example_en1: How long is the Rainbow Bridge?

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand picking 爫 fruit from a tree 木'}
grammar_note: 采取: Placed before measures or actions to indicate adoption or implementation.
example_zh1: 他们根据情报采取行动。
example_zh2: 我们采取了强有力的预防措施。
example_en2: We took strong measures to prevent it.
example_zh3: 接下来该采取什么行动就交给你了。
example_en3: I leave it in your hands what course of action to take.

grammar_note: 参考: Placed after nouns to indicate consulting or referring to them.
example_zh1: 汤姆很仔细地参考地图。
example_en1: Tom is looking closely at the map.
example_zh2: 在英国的时候，我经常看参考书。
example_en2: While in England I often consulted the guidebook.
example_zh3: 不留名或详细的参考什么都可以。
example_en3: Anonymity or detailed reference are both fine.

Translation: to take part; to participate in
grammar_note: 参与: Placed after subject to indicate participation in an activity.
惭愧: Used after verbs to express shame over actions or situations.
example_zh2: 我很惭愧，这是我第一次对我爸说谎。
example_en2: This is the first time I've ever lied to my father and I am ashamed of myself.

grammar_note: 操场: Placed after "在" to indicate a location for activities.
example_zh1: 操场上有很多孩子在玩耍。
example_en1: There are many children playing on the playground.
example_en2: We play basketball on the sports ground.
example_zh3: 每天早上，士兵们在操场上训练。
example_en3: Every morning, soldiers train on the drill ground.

Translation: to worry about; to take pains over; be concerned over
grammar_note: 操心: Placed after it to indicate worrying about someone or something.
example_en1: Be diligent, don't worry or be annoyed.
example_zh3: 別太操心了，不然會掉頭髮的。
example_en3: Don't worry too much, or you'll go bald.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'Bamboo strips 冂 tied together to form a book'}
grammar_note: 册: Used as a measure word for books or volumes in a noun phrase.
example_en1: Does it also work without registration?
example_en2: How many books does he have?

grammar_note: 测验: Used as a verb to indicate conducting a test or examination.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A rice cooker on heat 日, building up steam 丷 and letting it off'}
grammar_note: 曾经: Placed before a verb to indicate something happened in the past.
插: 动词，表示插入动作。

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Work 工 done by a sheep 羊; incompetence'}
grammar_note: 差别: Placed after nouns to indicate difference between them.
example_zh2: 两者之间有显著的差别。
example_en2: There are noticeable differences between the two.
example_zh3: 你知道显微镜和望远镜的差别吗？
example_en3: Do you know the difference between a microscope and a telescope?

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Work 工 done by a sheep 羊; incompetence'}
grammar_note: 差距: Placed after quantifiers to indicate a gap or disparity between two things.
example_zh1: 差距在他们之间越来越大了
example_en1: The gap between them is getting bigger and bigger.
example_zh2: 他的英语水平和我的有明显的差距。
example_en2: There is a noticeable disparity between his level of English and mine.
example_zh3: 我们需要缩小城乡之间的教育差距。
example_en3: We need to reduce the educational gap between urban and rural areas.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 又 grasping an object 丶'}
grammar_note: 叉子: A noun representing a fork used for eating.

Translation: to tear open; take apart; pull down
grammar_note: 拆: Placed as a verb to indicate dismantling or destroying something.
example_en3: How dare he open my letters!

grammar_note: 产品: Used as a noun to refer to goods or items produced.
example_en1: These products are of the same quality.
example_zh2: 这个产品是中国制造的。
example_en2: This product was made in China.
example_zh3: 这些产品的品质是一样的。
example_en3: The quality of these products is the same.

grammar_note: 产生: Placed after subject to indicate production or creation of something.
example_zh1: 有些药品会对身体产生危害。
example_en1: Some medicines can be harmful to the body.
example_zh2: 事故由一个简单的错误产生。
example_en2: The accident arose from a simple mistake.
example_zh3: 本世纪初以来，产生了很多进步。
example_en3: Many improvements have been made since this century began.

grammar_note: 常识: Used as a noun referring to general knowledge in a sentence.
example_en1: He is lacking in common sense.
example_en2: She is lacking in common sense.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 長; an old man with long hair and a cane'}
grammar_note: 长途: Used before nouns to describe long-distance travel or communication.
example_en1: Is she equal to a long journey?
example_zh3: 没有什么比坐长途汽车更无聊。
example_en3: Nothing is more boring than traveling long distances by car.

grammar_note: 抄: Placed after verbs to indicate copying or transcribing actions.
example_zh2: 在考试的时候，汤姆作弊抄了玛丽的答案。
example_en2: During the exam, Tom cheated off Mary.
example_zh3: 有時候我會想，翻譯這些連是自己母語的人都不甚了解，一看就知道是從哪本書上抄來的句子，它的意義到底在哪裡?
example_en3: Sometimes I wonder about the meaning of translating sentences that even native speakers don’t fully understand. It's clear they are sentences copied from some book; what is their true significance?

grammar_note: 超级: Placed before adjectives to intensify their meaning.
example_en2: I'm a huge fan of golf.
example_en3: Alexandre often goes to the supermarket.

grammar_note: 朝: Placed before nouns indicating dynasty, court, or government.
example_en3: I want to go to North Korea.

grammar_note: 潮湿: Used as an adjective to describe dampness or moisture in objects or environments.
example_zh1: 夏天总是闷热而又潮湿。
example_en1: Summer is always hot and humid.
example_zh2: 12月份巴厘岛极其炎热和潮湿。
example_en2: It is extremely hot and humid in Bali in December.
example_zh3: 这里的夏天很潮湿，另外，冬天很干燥。
example_en3: It gets very humid here in the summer. In the winter, on the other hand, it gets very dry.

grammar_note: 吵: Used as an adjective before nouns indicating noise or disturbance.
example_en2: There's a lot of noise here.

grammar_note: 炒: Placed as a verb indicating the cooking method of stir-frying.
example_en3: He's raking it in on the stock market.

grammar_note: 吵架: Used as a verb to indicate starting an argument.
example_en2: Did you have a fight with Ken?
example_en3: Did you have another fight with Tom?

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 車, a cart with two wheels, seen from above'}
grammar_note: 车库: Placed in a sentence as a noun indicating a specific location for vehicle storage.
example_en1: The car is in the garage.
example_en2: I forgot it in the garage.
example_zh3: 我把车库改造成工作室使用。
example_en3: I adapted the garage for use as a workshop.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 車, a cart with two wheels, seen from above'}
grammar_note: 车厢: Placed as a noun in sentences to denote railway carriage or compartment.
example_zh1: 汤姆在车厢里找到玛丽的雨伞。
example_en1: Tom found Mary's umbrella in the trunk of his car.

grammar_note: 彻底: Placed after an adjective to intensify its meaning thoroughly.

grammar_note: 单纯: Used as an adjective to describe simplicity or purity.
example_zh1: 我还记得我第一次去中国，我在山东，意识到那个单纯的省比英格兰大两万六千平方公里。
example_en1: I still remember the first time I was in China; I was in Shandong, and I realised that that province alone is twenty six thousand square kilometres bigger than England.

grammar_note: 单调: Used as an adjective to describe something monotonous or dull.
example_zh1: 我厌倦了现在单调的生活。
example_en1: I am tired of my monotonous life.

Translation: alone; by oneself; on one's own; single-handed
grammar_note: 单独: Placed before a verb to indicate doing something alone.
example_en1: I want him to do it alone.
example_zh2: 我想和汤姆单独谈一谈。
example_en2: I'd like to talk to Tom alone.
example_zh3: 汤姆和玛丽单独在一起。

Translation: assume the office of; to hold the post of
grammar_note: 担任: Placed before a role noun to indicate assuming that role.
example_zh1: 我很高兴我们录用了你来担任这份工作。
example_en1: I'm glad we hired you for this job.
example_zh2: 多亏了他的推荐，我得以在东京的一所大学里担任老师。
example_en2: It was all thanks to his recommendation that I was able to become a teacher at a college in Tokyo.

grammar_note: 单位: Placed after a quantifier to indicate organizational unit or workplace.
example_zh2: 模为1的向量是单位向量。
example_en2: A vector is a unit vector if its norm is 1.
example_zh3: 在我的单位，我是最年轻的。
example_en3: I'm the youngest in my department.

grammar_note: 耽误: Placed after verbs to indicate causing delays.
example_zh1: 可以耽误你一点时间吗?
example_zh2: 事故耽误了我们半小时。
example_en2: An accident delayed us for half an hour.
example_zh3: 我发现你玩绝对不耽误学习。我就不行。
example_en3: I've noticed that having fun doesn't interfere at all with your studies. I just can't.

grammar_note: 单元: Serves as a noun indicating a unit or cell in a structure or system.
example_zh2: 这个电路板上的单元坏了。
example_en2: The cell on this circuit board is broken.
example_zh3: 我们今天完成了这个课程的单元学习。
example_en3: We finished the unit of today's lesson.

grammar_note: 胆小鬼: Used as a noun to refer to someone who is cowardly.
example_en2: He is afraid of his own shadow.

grammar_note: 淡: Placed before nouns to describe thinness, light color, or lack of taste.
example_en3: I was very cold towards her.

grammar_note: 当地: Placed before nouns to indicate local area or locality.
example_zh2: 这家报社在当地知名度颇高。
example_en2: This newspaper is well known in the local area.
example_zh3: 汤姆参加了当地的一个自行车比赛
example_en3: Tom took part in a local bike race.

grammar_note: 当心: Used at the beginning of a sentence to warn someone to be careful.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 扌 raised at the right time 当; 当 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 挡: Placed before a verb to indicate blocking or hindering an action.

Translation: fall on hard times; have bad luck
grammar_note: 倒霉: Used as an adjective to describe being unlucky or having bad fortune.
example_en1: He is shit out of luck.
example_en2: He is shit out of luck.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 寸 pointing the way to someplace 巳'}
grammar_note: 导演: Serves as a noun referring to a person who directs films or plays.
example_zh2: 他是个富有才能的年轻导演。

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A bird 鸟 perched atop a mountain 山'}
grammar_note: 岛屿: A noun referring to islands and islets in a geographical context.
example_en1: There are islands in the sea.
example_zh3: 这个岛屿位于日本的西边。
example_en3: The island lies to the west of Japan.

Translation: to cause; lead to; result in
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 寸 pointing the way to someplace 巳'}
grammar_note: 导致: Placed after verbs to indicate causing something.
到达: Placed after verbs indicating movement to show arrival at a destination.
example_en2: The train is to arrive on time.

grammar_note: 道德: Serves as a noun expressing morality or ethics in a sentence.
example_zh1: 道德上的恶乃是无知的后果。
example_en1: Moral evil is the result of ignorance.
example_zh2: 为了救许多人牺牲一个人是否道德？
example_en2: Would it be ethical to sacrifice one person to save many?
example_zh3: 议员受到了议会道德委员会的谴责。
example_en3: The senator was censured by the congressional ethics committee.

grammar_note: 道理: Placed after nouns indicating the principle or reason behind them.
登记: Placed as a verb to indicate the action of registering or checking in.
example_zh2: 先生，请出示护照或者身份证，让我登记一下。
example_en2: Sir, please present your passport or identity card, so I can register it.
example_zh3: 当您登记美国大学时，您考TOEFL获得的分数只是所选因素的其中一个。
example_en3: When applying to American universities, your TOEFL score is only one factor.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Bamboo strips ⺮ laid before a court 寺'}
grammar_note: 等待: Placed as a main verb to indicate waiting for someone or something.

Translation: equal to; equivalent to; be worth
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Bamboo strips ⺮ laid before a court 寺'}
grammar_note: 等于: Placed between nouns to indicate equivalence.
example_en1: Subtract two from ten and you have eight.

grammar_note: 滴: Used as a measure word for small droplets or amounts.
example_en1: Constant dripping wears away a stone.
example_en2: Constant dripping wears away a stone.

grammar_note: 的确: Placed before a verb or proposition to emphasize certainty.
example_en1: It is true that television also has some disadvantages.
example_zh2: 我抓不到句子的确切含义。
example_en2: I can't get at the exact meaning of the sentence.
example_zh3: 汤姆的确是个很会讲话的人。
example_en3: Tom certainly is an eloquent speaker.

grammar_note: 敌人: Used as a noun to refer to an enemy or foe in a sentence.

Translation: to hand over; to pass on; progressively
grammar_note: 递: Placed after direct object to indicate passing or handing over an item.
地道: Placed before nouns to indicate authenticity or typicality of something from a place.
example_en1: She had the decency to apologize.
example_zh3: 这样说是不是更加地道呢？
example_en3: Is it more idiomatic if I say it like this?

Translation: geographical features of a place; geography
grammar_note: 地理: Serves as a subject or object in sentences discussing geographical topics.
example_zh3: 變音符號有助於更準確地理解文字。
example_en3: Tashkil helps in understanding texts more precisely.

grammar_note: 地区: Placed after verbs to specify area or region involved.
example_en2: The typhoon struck the Kanto district.
example_zh3: 这是一个产苹果的地区。
example_en3: Apples are produced in this district.

grammar_note: 地毯: A noun representing a carpet or rug in a sentence.
example_en3: The dog was sleeping on the mat.

grammar_note: 地位: Placed after nouns indicating one's standing or status in a context.
example_zh1: 罗伯特满足于现在的地位。
example_en1: Robert is content with his present position.
example_zh2: 他給了湯姆一個重要的地位。
example_en2: He gave Tom an important position.
example_zh3: 他们很明显在嫉妒他的财富和地位。
example_en3: Obviously, they are jealous of his wealth and status.

grammar_note: 地震: Used as a noun to describe an earthquake event.
example_en3: There are many earthquakes in Japan.

grammar_note: 点心: A noun referring to snacks or dim sum in a sentence.
example_en2: I love the Dim sims from Tim Ho Wan.
example_en3: I'm tired, and a bit annoyed.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 電; lightning 申 from a storm cloud 雨'}
grammar_note: 电池: Used as a noun referring to a battery or cell in a sentence.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 電; lightning 申 from a storm cloud 雨'}
grammar_note: 电台: Serves as a noun referring to a radio station or transceiver in sentences.

Translation: fish with a hook and line; angle
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A metal 钅 hook 勺; 勺 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 钓: Used as a verb to indicate the action of fishing with a line and hook.

Translation: apex; [measure word for something with a top (e.g. hat, tent, etc.)]
grammar_note: 顶: Used as a measure word for items with a top or apex.
example_en1: He is used to talking back.
example_en2: What is the price of this cap?
example_en3: The King of France is bald.

grammar_note: 洞: A noun indicating a hole or cavity in a sentence.
冻: Used as a verb to describe the state of being frozen or making something jelly-like.
动画片: A noun referring to cartoons, used as a subject or object in sentences.
example_zh1: 现在的日本动画片越来越色情了！
example_en1: Japanese anime these days is becoming more and more like pornography.
example_zh2: 我想学日语，但是我不喜欢看日本动画片。
example_en2: I want to learn Japanese but I don't like watching anime.

grammar_note: 逗: Placed before a noun to indicate teasing or playing with something/someone.
example_en2: I love to make people laugh.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'An old serving dish 口 on a stand with a lid 一'}
grammar_note: 豆腐: A noun representing bean curd or tofu in a sentence.

Translation: stand alone; independent; on one's own
grammar_note: 独立: Can function as an adjective meaning independent or as a verb meaning to stand alone.
example_en1: You have to do it by yourself.

grammar_note: 独特: Used as an adjective to describe something unique or distinctive.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Twenty 廿 people 又 meeting inside a building 广 to deliberate'}
grammar_note: 度过: Followed by a noun indicating how time is spent.
example_en1: The danger has not passed yet.
example_en2: He spent the evening reading a book.
example_zh3: 你度过愉快的时光了吗？
example_en3: Did you have a good time?

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Using an axe 斤 to harvest grain 米'}
grammar_note: 断: Placed after verbs to indicate breaking or severing something.
堆: Used as a verb to pile up objects or as a measure word for abstract quantities.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A pair 又 of hands 寸'}
grammar_note: 对比: Placed after nouns to form phrases indicating comparison or contrast.
example_zh1: 新的旗袍又修长又紧身，也有短裙摆，与传统式样构成了鲜明的对比。
example_en1: Slender and form-fitting with a high cut, the new qipao contrasted sharply with the traditional one.

Translation: to treat; handle; be in a position related to another
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A pair 又 of hands 寸'}
grammar_note: 对待: Followed by a noun indicating how one treats or handles something/someone.
example_zh2: 为什么他要这么对待你？
example_en2: Why did he treat you like that?
example_zh3: 我不喜欢他怎么对待他人。
example_en3: I do not like the way he treats others.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A pair 又 of hands 寸'}
grammar_note: 对方: Used as a noun to refer to the other party in communication or interaction.
example_en2: Tom and I splashed each other.
example_zh3: 他们互相送礼物给对方。
example_en3: They give presents to one another.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A beast 兄 with two horns 丷'}
grammar_note: 兑换: Placed after objects to indicate exchanging them.
example_zh1: 兑换是一种常见的行为。
example_zh3: 我可以用积分兑换礼品。
example_en3: I can exchange my points for gifts.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A pair 又 of hands 寸'}
grammar_note: 对手: Placed after verbs indicating actions against opponents.
example_zh3: 他对自己的对手门很大度。
example_en3: He is generous to his opponents.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A pair 又 of hands 寸'}
grammar_note: 对象: Used after descriptors to indicate a specific partner or target.
example_en2: The book's target audience is primary school students.
example_en3: He is looking for his life partner as an object of affection.

grammar_note: 吨: Placed after numerals to measure weight in tons.
example_en1: This grizzly bear weighs half a ton.
example_en2: We'd like to order 18 tonnes of olive oil.
example_zh3: 这辆卡车最大的载重量是5吨。
example_en3: This truck has a maximum load of 5 tons.

Translation: squat on the heels; to crouch
grammar_note: 蹲: Placed as a verb indicating the action of squatting or crouching.
example_zh1: 湯姆蹲了三年多的監獄。
example_en1: Tom spent more than three years in jail.
example_zh2: 搶劫銀行的後果就是在監獄裏蹲十年。
example_en2: Bank robbery will cost you ten years in prison.

Translation: [measure word for occurences, and therefore of meals]
grammar_note: 顿: Placed after nouns indicating meals or events to measure occurrences.
example_en3: What time is it in Boston?

grammar_note: 多亏: Placed at the beginning of a sentence to express gratitude or relief due to something.
example_en2: I owe it you that I am still alive.
example_en3: Thanks to you I've lost my appetite.

grammar_note: 多余: Placed after a noun to indicate something is unnecessary or surplus.
example_en2: Do you have an extra key?
example_zh3: 事实证明了我们的担心是多余的。
example_en3: The facts proved that our worries were unnecessary.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Flowers 几 blooming on a tree 木'}
grammar_note: 朵: Placed before flower nouns to measure them.
example_en1: I have an itch in my ear.

Translation: to hide oneself; go into hiding
grammar_note: 躲藏: 动词，表示隐藏的动作。
example_zh2: Shh！不要出聲……我們現在捉迷藏，要搞的話快點找一個地方躲藏一邊了。
example_en2: Shh! Don't make a sound. We are playing hide-and-seek now. If you want to talk, go find somewhere else to hide.

grammar_note: 恶劣: Placed after nouns to describe vile or odious conditions.
example_zh1: 今天天气比昨天恶劣多了。
example_en1: Today's weather is much worse than yesterday's.
example_zh2: 由于天气恶劣，飞机延误了。
example_en2: Due to bad weather, the plane was late.
example_zh3: 恶劣的天气对他的健康带来了影响。
example_en3: The bad weather affected his health.

grammar_note: 耳环: A noun referring to earrings, used as a standalone object.
example_zh3: 她今天戴着新买的耳环。
example_en3: She is wearing new earrings today.

grammar_note: 发表: Placed after verbs to indicate issuing or publishing something.
example_zh2: 他刚发表一系列有趣的文章。
example_en2: He has just published an interesting series of articles.
example_zh3: 文章的发表被预定在教授生日那天。
example_en3: Publication of the article was timed to coincide with the professor's birthday.

Translation: to worry; to be anxious; sullen
grammar_note: 发愁: Used as a verb to express worry or anxiety about something.
发达: Placed after nouns to describe development or advancement status.
example_zh1: 一般说来，男生的肌肉比女生发达。
example_en1: Generally speaking, men are physically stronger than women.
example_zh2: 中国大陆的沿海城市普遍比内陆城市发达。
example_en2: Chinese coastal cities are generally more developed than the inland ones.
example_zh3: 因为缺乏的政府的关注，这个区域还不发达。
example_en3: This area is still underdeveloped because of a lack of interest from the government.

grammar_note: 发抖: Placed in a sentence as a verb indicating trembling or shivering.
example_zh2: 我的身体被冻得瑟瑟发抖。
example_zh3: 令人震惊的光景让了他吓得发抖。
example_en3: The terrible scene made him tremble in fear.

Translation: bring into play; give free rein to
grammar_note: 发挥: Placed after verbs to indicate utilization or full expression of abilities/talents.
example_zh2: 汤姆最近在工作中发挥不太好。
example_en2: Tom has not been doing very well at work recently.
example_zh3: 为了保持竞争力，我们得发挥我们的优势。
example_en3: To remain competitive, we've got to play to our strengths.

grammar_note: 发明: Used as a verb to indicate inventing something or as a noun for an invention.
发票: Used after transactions to refer to the bill or receipt issued.

Translation: speak; make a statement; take the floor
grammar_note: 发言: Placed after subject to indicate making a speech or statement.
example_en1: Who is going to speak tonight?
example_en2: All at once, he spoke out.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 罰; to punish 刂 the accused 詈'}
grammar_note: 罚款: Used as a verb to impose a fine or as a noun referring to the fine itself.
example_zh1: 在新加坡的街道上扔垃圾会被罚款。
example_en1: They fine you in Singapore if you throw trash in the streets.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'The course 去 followed by a stream 氵'}
grammar_note: 法院: Serves as a noun referring to a legal court in sentences.
example_zh1: 被告会向上级法院上诉。
example_en1: The defendant will appeal to a higher court.
example_zh2: 大使馆就在最高法院旁边。
example_en2: The embassy is located next to the Supreme Court.
example_zh3: 法院判决了那个遗言是有效的。
example_en3: The court adjudged that the will was valid.

grammar_note: 翻: Placed before verbs to indicate actions of turning over or reversing something.
繁荣: Used as an adjective to describe flourishing or prosperous conditions.
example_en1: For how long did the Maya culture flourish?
example_zh2: 上海那么繁荣，主要是一百六十年前开埠以后发生的变化。
example_en2: Shanghai is so prosperous; notably it was after the port was opened for trade one hundred and sixty years ago that things started to change.
example_zh3: 让我们记住这一点，如果说这场金融危机教会了我们什么东西的话，那就是我们不可能在金融以外的领域处于困境的同时拥有繁荣兴旺的华尔街。
example_en3: Let us remember that if this financial crisis taught us anything, it's that we cannot have a thriving Wall Street while Main Street suffers.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 又 held up against a cliff 厂'}
grammar_note: 反而: Placed before a contrasting idea to indicate the opposite of expected results.
example_zh1: 她不仅没责怪他，反而称赞他。
example_en1: It wasn't just that she didn't blame him - she actually praised the guy.
example_zh2: 发泄很少改善我的情绪，反而经常使它更糟。
example_en2: Venting rarely improves my mood and often makes it worse.
example_zh3: 你不但不和我一起吃饭，反而去和另一个女生吃饭！
example_en3: Not only did you not eat with me, you went to have dinner with another girl!

Translation: repeatedly; again and again; over and over
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 又 held up against a cliff 厂'}
grammar_note: 反复: Placed before verbs to indicate repetition of actions.
example_zh1: 他在心里反复思量这件事。
example_en1: He turned over the matter in his mind.
example_zh2: 我知道自己是个累赘，你没必要反复提。
example_en2: I know I'm a burden; you don't have to repeat it.
example_zh3: 我辗转反侧，反复思考着白天发生的事，后悔不已。
example_en3: I'm tossing and turning, repeatedly thinking about what happened today, deeply remorseful.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 又 held up against a cliff 厂'}
grammar_note: 反应: 可用作动词表示回应，或名词指反应、后果。
example_en2: Tom was too surprised to react.
example_zh3: 原子反应堆发出大量的热能。
example_en3: The atomic reactor generates enormous amounts of thermal energy.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 又 held up against a cliff 厂'}
grammar_note: 反映: Placed after verbs to indicate reflection or representation of something.
example_zh2: 我的眼睛是一片反映我梦想的海洋。
example_en2: My eyes are an ocean in which my dreams are reflected.
example_zh3: 一个国家的风俗习惯反映了它的文化。
example_en3: The manners and customs of a country reflect its culture.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand 又 held up against a cliff 厂'}
grammar_note: 反正: Placed at the beginning of a clause to mean 'anyway' or 'in any case'.
example_zh3: 反正你想来天津玩跟我说。
example_en3: In any case, just tell me if you want to come to Tianjin for a vacation.

grammar_note: 范围: Placed after nouns to indicate scope or extent of a topic.
example_zh1: 这份工作在我能力范围之外.
example_en1: This job is beyond my ability.
example_zh2: 他试图扩大自己的势力范围。
example_en2: He tried to enlarge his sphere of influence.
example_zh3: 专家就是一个能够把所有的错误控制在最小范围内的人。
example_en3: An expert is a person who has made all the mistakes that can be made in a very narrow field.

grammar_note: 方：放在时间词前表示“刚刚”。
方案: Placed after verbs related to creation or discussion to refer to plans or schemes.
example_en2: That sounds like a fairly good proposal.

grammar_note: 妨碍: Placed after subjects to indicate hindering actions or states.
example_en2: The strike affected the nation's economy.
example_zh3: 暴风妨碍了我们准时到达。
example_en3: The storm prevented us from arriving on time.

Translation: to seem as if; be more or less the same; be alike
grammar_note: 仿佛: Placed before a clause to indicate seeming as if.
example_zh1: 那一刻，时间仿佛静止了。
example_en1: At that moment, time seemed to stand still.
example_zh2: 他讲起那场事故，讲得仿佛他亲眼所见。
example_en2: He recounted the accident to me as if he had seen it with his own eyes.
example_zh3: 在他们双目交接的瞬间，世界仿佛静止了。
example_en3: When their eyes met, it was as if the world stood still.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': "Two bird's wings opposed; two people back-to-back"}
grammar_note: 非: Placed before verbs/adjectives to negate them, similar to 不 but more formal.
肥皂: A noun representing soap, used as a subject or object in sentences.
example_en3: He got shampoo in his eyes.

grammar_note: 废话: Used as a noun to refer to unnecessary speech or nonsense.
example_zh2: 我曾说过的废话当中那是最愚蠢的一句。
example_en2: That's the stupidest thing I've ever said.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Pieces 八 being further subdivided with a knife 刀 '}
grammar_note: 分别: Placed after verbs to indicate separation or distinction.
example_zh1: 每堂课我都分别有一本笔记。
example_en1: I have a separate notebook for each class.
example_zh2: Fred来不来聚会对我来说没分别。
example_en2: It makes no difference to me whether Fred came to the party or not.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Pieces 八 being further subdivided with a knife 刀 '}
grammar_note: 分布: Used as a verb to describe the spread or distribution of something.
example_zh1: 在图形上，正态分布是一种钟形曲线，越接近中心，取值越大，越远离中心，取值越小。
example_en1: In its graphical representation, the normal distribution is a bell-shaped curve, with the value growing as one moves closer to the middle and decreasing as one moves away.

grammar_note: 纷纷: Placed after verbs to indicate many people doing something successively.
example_zh1: 在美国，由于投资者纷纷涌向包括黄金和美国国债在内的安全港，因此主要的股票市场指数在星期一一度下跌了3个百分点。
example_en1: In the United States, the major stock market indices at one point were down three percentage points on Monday, as investors rushed to safe havens, including gold and U.S. Treasury bonds.
example_zh2: 在美国，由于投资者纷纷涌向包括黄金和美国国债在内的安全港，因此主要的股票价格指数在星期一一度下跌了3个百分点。
example_en2: In the United States, the major stock market indices at one point were down three percentage points on Monday, as investors rushed to safe havens, including gold and U.S. Treasury bonds.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Pieces 八 being further subdivided with a knife 刀 '}
grammar_note: 分配: Placed as a verb to indicate the act of distributing or allocating something.
example_en1: From each according to their ability, to each according to their needs.
example_zh2: 現在不止要男女薪金平等，而且還要平均分配家務。
example_en2: It is time not only to equalize men's and women's wages, but also to equalize responsibility for housework.
example_zh3: 自由职业的优点是，人们可以自由的分配他们的工作时间。它的缺点是，人们实际上必须24小时不间断的工作。
example_en3: The advantage of freelancing is that you can divide your time freely. The disadvantage is that you actually have to work around the clock.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Pieces 八 being further subdivided with a knife 刀 '}
grammar_note: 分手: Used as a verb to indicate the end of a relationship.
example_en2: I mean to break up with her.
example_en3: I want to break up with you.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Pieces 八 being further subdivided with a knife 刀 '}
grammar_note: 分析: 动词，表示进行分析的动作。
example_en1: How do you parse this sentence?
example_zh2: 汤姆是一名金融分析师。
example_zh3: 我们已经将它做了分析。

Translation: struggle; to fight for; to strive for
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A man 大 working on the farm 田'}
grammar_note: 奋斗: Placed as a verb to express striving or struggling for something.
example_en2: I am fighting for my future.

grammar_note: 风格: Placed after adjectives or nouns to describe style or form.
example_zh1: 你想要哪种风格的家具？
example_en1: What style of furniture would you like?
example_en2: She had an individual style of speaking.
example_zh3: 你喜欢什么风格的音乐？
example_en3: What kind of music do you like?

grammar_note: 风景: Serves as a noun representing scenery in sentences.
example_en1: Tom needs a change of scenery.
example_en2: The landscape is unfamiliar to me.
example_zh3: 这个地方以风景优美闻名。
example_en3: This place is famous for its scenic beauty.

grammar_note: 疯狂: Used as an adjective to describe something or someone being insane or frenzied.
example_zh3: 有时候， Dennis真的很疯狂。

grammar_note: 风俗: A noun referring to customs or traditions in a place or culture.
example_zh1: 风俗习惯包括食物，庆祝和舞蹈。
example_en1: Customs include food, celebrations and dancing.
example_zh2: 一个国家的风俗习惯反映了它的文化。
example_en2: The manners and customs of a country reflect its culture.

grammar_note: 风险: Placed as a noun in sentences to indicate risk or danger.
example_en3: I don't worry about the risk.

grammar_note: 讽刺: Used as a verb to express mockery or sarcasm towards someone or something.
example_en1: Satire is a way of expression.
example_zh3: 他用讽刺的话来回应批评。
example_en3: He responded to criticism with sarcastic remarks.

grammar_note: 否定: Used before verbs to negate them.
example_en1: No one can deny the fact.
example_zh2: 汤姆认为答案是否定的。
example_en2: Tom thinks the answer is no.
example_zh3: 他怎麼否定上帝的存在。
example_en3: How can he deny God's existence?

grammar_note: 否认: Placed after verbs to negate them, specifically in denying facts or承认的事物.
example_en1: He denied having stolen the money.
example_en2: Tom denied having stolen the money.

Translation: hold up; support with the hand; to help somebody up
grammar_note: 扶: Placed before a verb to indicate supporting or helping someone up.
example_en2: You can't raise a cat to be a dog.
example_zh3: 我們買了張舒適的扶手椅。
example_en3: We bought a comfortable new armchair.

Translation: width of cloth; [measure word (for paintings, pictures, textiles etc.)]
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A roll 畐 of cloth 巾; 畐 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 幅: Placed before paintings or textiles to measure them.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A person 卩 putting on 又 a coat 月'}
grammar_note: 服装: A noun representing clothing or attire in a sentence.
example_zh1: 这家精品店的服装卖得很贵.
example_en1: The clothes at this boutique are particularly expensive.
example_zh2: 不能根据服装来判断一个人。
example_en2: You can't judge a person based on clothing.
example_zh3: 这几套衣服是同一位服装师设计的.
example_en3: These dresses were designed by the same designer.

grammar_note: 辅导: Placed after subject to indicate coaching or tutoring activity.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 婦; a woman 女 with a broom 彐'}
grammar_note: 妇女: Noun referring to women, used in formal contexts.
example_en3: Women have the right to choose.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A person 亻 who goes  somewhere 夂 every day 日'}
grammar_note: 复制: Placed as a verb to indicate duplicating or copying something.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand with a stick 攵 disciplining a kneeling child 己'}
grammar_note: 改革: Placed as a verb to indicate implementing reform.
example_en3: They were busy working for social reforms.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand with a stick 攵 disciplining a kneeling child 己'}
grammar_note: 改进: Used as a verb to express making something better or improving it.
example_en1: Your essay still needs some improvement.
example_zh2: 近来各方面都有所改进。
example_zh3: 改革者的目标是要改进政府。
example_en3: Reformers aim to improve the government.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand with a stick 攵 disciplining a kneeling child 己'}
grammar_note: 改善: Placed after subject to indicate improving something.
example_zh3: 我努力地改善我的成績。
example_en3: I made efforts to improve my grades.

Translation: to correct; to amend; put right
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand with a stick 攵 disciplining a kneeling child 己'}
grammar_note: 改正: Placed after verbs to indicate correcting or amending actions.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A dish 皿 with a lid 羊'}
grammar_note: 盖: Placed before a verb to indicate covering or closing something.
example_en3: Tom put a cover over his car.

grammar_note: 概括: Placed as a verb to summarize or generalize content.
example_zh1: 美國是一個可以用一個字來概括的國家。我曾與習近平主席一起在喜馬拉雅山麓。
example_en1: America is a nation that can be defined in a single word. I was in the foothills of the Himalayas with Xi Jinping.

grammar_note: 概念: Placed as a noun to express a concept or idea.
example_zh2: 关于这个我几乎没什么概念。
example_en2: I know almost nothing about it.
example_zh3: 我觉得这个网站的概念非常好。
example_en3: I really like the concept of this website.

grammar_note: 干脆: Placed before verbs to add meaning of decisiveness or straightforwardness.
example_en1: You might as well come, too.
example_zh2: 他跟他们干脆地断绝来往了。
example_en2: He made a clean break with them.
example_zh3: 世上所有问题都可以用下面三种方式解决：接受，改变，或是干脆放开。
example_en3: There are three solutions to every problem: accept it, change it or leave it.

grammar_note: 干燥: Placed after nouns to describe dry conditions or states.
example_zh1: 这是片干燥地区，几乎是一片荒漠。
example_en1: It is an arid region, almost a desert.
example_zh2: 这里的夏天很潮湿，另外，冬天很干燥。
example_en2: It gets very humid here in the summer. In the winter, on the other hand, it gets very dry.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Two hearts 心 beating together 咸'}
grammar_note: 感激: Placed after a verb to express feeling grateful for something received.

Translation: at once; losing no time; hasten
grammar_note: 赶紧: Placed before a verb to urge immediate action.
赶快: Placed before a verb to urge immediate action.
example_en3: The sooner he shuts up, the better.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Two hearts 心 beating together 咸'}
grammar_note: 感受: Can function as a verb (to feel/perceive) or noun (feeling/perception).

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Two hearts 心 beating together 咸'}
grammar_note: 感想: Placed after experiences to express thoughts or reflections.
example_zh1: 你对这一切有什么感想？
example_en1: How did you feel about all that?
example_zh2: 你對這場比賽有甚麼感想？
example_en2: How did you feel about the game?

Translation: to work [often manual] on a job
grammar_note: 干活儿: To work, often manually; used as a verb in sentences indicating doing manual labor.
example_zh3: 她每天早上六点开始干活儿。
example_en3: She starts working at six in the morning every day.

grammar_note: 钢铁: Serves as a noun representing iron and steel in a sentence.

example_en1: There are daisies next to the steel building.
example_zh2: 那里有许多雏菊围绕着钢铁大厦。
example_en2: There are daisies around the steel building.

grammar_note: 高档: Used as an adjective before nouns indicating high quality or superior grade.
example_zh1: 汤姆和玛丽入住了一家高档酒店。
example_en1: Tom and Mary stayed at a fancy hotel.

grammar_note: 高级: Placed before nouns to indicate high level or advanced nature.
example_zh1: 英国皇家的一位高级人员告诉了CNN，剑桥公爵夫人嫁给威廉王子 一年之后，达到了所有的目标，并且成功地成为了英国皇室的“正式成员”。
example_en1: A senior royal told CNN that the Duchess of Cambridge has fulfilled all of her objectives one year after marrying Prince William and has become a "full member" of the British monarchy.

Translation: to make/do; carry on; be engaged in
grammar_note: 搞: Used as a verb to express making/doings engaging in activities.

Translation: bid farewell to; to say good-bye to
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To speak 口 with the force of an ox 牛'}
grammar_note: 告别: Placed after a preposition or used alone as a verb to indicate saying farewell.
example_en1: He bade farewell to the students.

grammar_note: 隔壁: Placed before a noun to indicate the adjacent location.
example_en1: He lives next door to us.
example_en2: She lives next door to him.

grammar_note: 格外: Placed before adjectives to intensify meaning.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A tally 丨 of people 人'}
grammar_note: 个别: Placed before nouns to indicate individuality or particular cases.
example_zh1: 只有个别人才懂了我的意思。
example_en1: Only a few people understood me.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A tally 丨 of people 人'}
grammar_note: 个人: Placed before nouns to indicate personal possession or individuality.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A tally 丨 of people 人'}
grammar_note: 个性: Placed after adjectives or used alone as a noun to discuss personality traits.
example_zh2: 我的个性还有很多方面是你不了解的。
example_en2: There are a lot of things you don't know about my personality.

grammar_note: 各自: Placed before nouns to indicate individual actions or states.
example_zh1: 請回到你們各自的座位。
example_zh2: 幸福家庭的幸福原因全都大同小異，但悲慘的家庭卻往往各自有各自的慘法。
example_en2: All happy families resemble each other, each unhappy family is unhappy in its own way.

Translation: root; descendants; completely; [measure word for long, slender objects]
grammar_note: 根: Used as a measure word for long, slender objects.
example_en2: Shall I put in a few cucumbers?
example_en3: I don't believe it at all.

grammar_note: 根本: Placed before verbs/adjectives to emphasize fundamental nature.
example_en1: I don't believe it at all.
example_en3: It's not a dream at all.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To divide 八 what is private 厶'}

example_en2: Algeria has unveiled a new economic plan.
example_zh3: 南非近 70 萬名高中生一直熱切期盼著本週公布他們的畢業考試成績，大學會根據這些成績來決定學生可以進入哪個專業學習。
example_en3: South Africa’s nearly 700,000 high-schoolers had been eagerly awaiting this week’s announcement of their matriculation exam grades—scores used by universities to determine which program of study a student is admitted to.

grammar_note: 工厂: Serves as a noun representing a place of industrial production.

example_en3: My father works at a factory.

grammar_note: 工程师: Serves as a noun indicating a person's profession in engineering.
工具: A noun representing any implement or device used to perform tasks.
example_en1: The carpenter brought his tools along.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To divide 八 what is private 厶'}
grammar_note: 公开: Can function as a verb to make something public or an adjective meaning overt.

example_zh3: 公开表示你对某人的爱。
example_en3: Publicly express your love for someone.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Results produced by capable 力 labor 工; 工 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 功能: Placed after adjectives or verbs to indicate capability or utility.

example_en3: The function of the brake is to stop the car.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To divide 八 what is private 厶'}
grammar_note: 公平: Used as an adjective to describe fairness or justice in situations or actions.
工人: Functions as a noun referring to a worker or labourer in sentences.
恭喜: Placed before a noun to express congratulations.
工业: Serves as a noun representing an industry in a sentence.

example_zh3: 该地区因它的手工业而出名。

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To divide 八 what is private 厶'}
grammar_note: 公寓: Used as a noun referring to apartments or flats in a sentence.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To divide 八 what is private 厶'}
grammar_note: 公元: Placed before years to denote the Christian/Common era.

example_en1: First came the Celts in 600 B.C.
example_zh2: 公元前七千年那段时间发生了很多重要的历史事件。
example_en2: Many important historical events took place 7000 years B.C.
example_zh3: 普遍认为佛教公元六七年在东汉明帝的统治时先来中国。
example_en3: It is generally believed that Buddhism first came to China in 67 A.D. during the reign of Emperor Mingdi of the Eastern Han Dynasty.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To divide 八 what is private 厶'}
grammar_note: 公主: Noun referring to a princess, used as a subject or object in sentences.

example_en3: The grand prize is a kiss from the princess.

grammar_note: 贡献: Placed after verbs indicating what is dedicated or contributed.

grammar_note: 沟通: Placed as a verb to indicate communication or connection between subjects.

example_en2: When an Uyghur met a Belarusian, what language did the two speak to each other?

grammar_note: 构成: Placed after nouns to indicate formation or composition.

example_zh3: 灵魂是由理性、意志和情欲构成的。
example_en3: The soul is made up of reason, determination, and passion.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'An older 古 woman 女; 古 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 姑姑: A noun referring to one's paternal aunt.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'An older 古 woman 女; 古 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 姑娘: A noun referring to a young unmarried woman or girl.
example_en1: Don't get sassy with me young lady!
example_en2: You're the most beautiful girl in the world.
example_zh3: 你們這些姑娘在做甚麼？

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Words passing through ten 十 mouths 口'}
grammar_note: 古代: Placed before nouns to indicate ancient times or antiquity.

example_zh2: 我父親對古代歷史有興趣。
example_en2: My father is interested in ancient history.
example_zh3: 羅馬以其古代建築而聞名。
example_en3: Rome is famous for its ancient architecture.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Words passing through ten 十 mouths 口'}
grammar_note: 古典: Used as an adjective before nouns to describe classical nature.
股票: A noun representing shares or stock in a company.
example_en1: He lost a fortune in the stock market.
example_en2: He invested his money in stocks.
example_zh3: 股票價格跌至歷史新低。
example_en3: Stock prices plunged to a record low.

grammar_note: 骨头: Serves as a noun representing bone in sentences.
example_en1: Bones are part of the body.
example_en2: The dog's bone was picked up.
example_en3: He accidentally bit into a bone while eating meat.

grammar_note: 鼓舞: Placed after subject to indicate inspiring or encouraging someone.

example_en3: I cheered myself up by listening to music.

grammar_note: 鼓掌: Placed as a verb to indicate the action of applauding.
固定: Placed before nouns to indicate something is fixed or set.

example_zh2: 你有一个固定的男朋友吗？
example_en2: Do you have a steady boyfriend?
example_zh3: 專職作家沒有固定的收入。
example_en3: Professional writers do not have a regular income.

grammar_note: 挂号: Placed after subject to indicate registering for services.
example_en2: I went to the hospital to register.
example_zh3: 医生说我需要先挂号才能看病。
example_en3: The doctor said I need to register first before seeing him.

grammar_note: 乖: Placed after a noun to describe someone as well-behaved.

Translation: to turn a corner; turn round; pursue a new course
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'To take another 另 by force 扌'}
grammar_note: 拐弯: 动词，表示转向或改变方向。

example_zh2: 你到这儿拐弯角上去坐地铁。
example_en2: Turn here to get on the subway.
example_zh3: 往北拐弯走到第二条弄堂就是。
example_en3: Turn north, walk to the second alley, and you're there.

grammar_note: 怪不得: Placed at the beginning of a sentence to express realization or understanding.

grammar_note: 官: Denotes a government official in a nominal phrase.
example_en3: James Cameron personally did the official promotion!

grammar_note: 关闭: Placed after subject to indicate closing action.
观察: Placed as a verb to indicate the act of observing or watching something.

example_en2: The woman observes and the man thinks.
example_en3: The boy observed the birds all day.

grammar_note: 观点: Serves as a noun expressing one's perspective or stance in discussions.
example_en1: Opinions vary from person to person.
example_en2: Why are you asking my opinion?
example_en3: I understood Tom's point of view.

grammar_note: 观念: Placed in subject position to express a concept or idea.

example_zh2: 没有经过仔细审视的观念是不值得拥有的，正如没有经过仔细审视的生活不值得过一样。
example_en2: An idea not properly analyzed is not worth exploiting, just as a life without self-judgment is not worth living.

grammar_note: 管子: Noun referring to a tube, pipe, or valve in a sentence.
example_en1: Something is stuck in the pipe.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A man 元 puts on a cap 冖 with his hand 寸'}
grammar_note: 冠军: Serves as a noun indicating the winner in a competition.

example_zh2: 只有一个人能成为世界冠军。问题是：会是谁呢？
example_en2: There can only be one world champion. The question is: Who will it be?

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A person 儿 carrying a torch 火'}
grammar_note: 光滑: Used as an adjective before nouns to describe smoothness or glossiness.

example_zh3: 它像婴儿的屁股一样光滑。
example_en3: It's as smooth as a baby's bottom.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A person 儿 carrying a torch 火'}
grammar_note: 光临: Used politely to welcome guests, placed after the subject.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A person 儿 carrying a torch 火'}
