grammar_note: 驾驶: Placed as a main verb indicating the action of driving or piloting.
example_en1: He was driving the car at full speed.
example_en3: I'm learning to drive at a driving school.

grammar_note: 价值: Placed after measure words or as subject/predicate to discuss worth or cost.
example_en1: This article is of no value.
example_en2: Do you know the value of fear?

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A man bringing home meat ⺼ for the family 户'}
grammar_note: 肩膀: A noun referring to the shoulder, used as a subject or object in sentences.
example_en2: He was wounded in the shoulder.

grammar_note: 艰巨: Placed after nouns to describe arduous tasks or formidable challenges.
example_zh1: 我老板把艰巨的任务指派给了我。
example_en1: My boss assigned the hard job to me.
example_zh2: 我知道你们的所做的一切并不只是为了赢得选举，我也知道你们做这一切并不是为了我。你们这样做是因为你们明白前面的任务有多么艰巨。即便我们今晚欢呼庆祝，我们也知道明天将面临我们一生之中最艰难的挑战——两场战争、一个面临危险的星球，一个世纪以来最严重的金融危机。
example_en2: And I know you didn't do this just to win an election. And I know you didn't do it for me. You did it because you understand the enormity of the task that lies ahead. For even as we celebrate tonight, we know the challenges that tomorrow will bring are the greatest of our lifetime: two wars, a planet in peril, the worst financial crisis in a century.

grammar_note: 坚决: Used before verbs to express firm determination or resoluteness.
example_en2: He is resolute in his attitude

grammar_note: 艰苦: Used as an adjective to describe arduous conditions or experiences.
example_zh2: 不管训练多么艰苦，她都没有哭过。
example_en2: No matter how hard the training was, she never cried.
example_zh3: 这不公平！凭什么我必须做艰苦的工作。
example_en3: It's not fair! I have to do the hard work!

grammar_note: 坚强: Used as an adjective to describe someone or something being strong or firm.
example_zh2: 生活很困难，但我更坚强。
example_en2: Life is hard, but I am harder.
example_zh3: 他很坚强，不会那么容易灰心。
example_en3: He won't be easily discouraged, because he's a tough guy.

Translation: hold two or more posts concurrently; part-time job
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A hand holding two sheafs of grain 禾'}
grammar_note: 兼职: Used as a noun to refer to part-time work or concurrent positions.
example_zh1: 她以前是兼职厨师，后来做了全职。
example_en1: She used to be a part time chef, then she became full time.
example_zh2: 你做那份兼职工作最多能赚到八万日元。
example_en2: You can make up to 80,000 yen a month in that part-time job.

Translation: to pick up; collect; to gather
grammar_note: 捡: Placed after subject to indicate picking up or collecting objects.
example_zh3: 我在海边捡了个漂亮贝壳。
example_en3: I picked up a pretty shell at the seaside.

grammar_note: 剪刀: A noun representing scissors or shears in a sentence.
example_en2: Use scissors to cut out the pictures.

grammar_note: 简历: Used as a noun to refer to a document summarizing one's education and work experience.
example_zh1: 我根本不在乎我的简历。
example_en1: I don't give a damn about my CV.

grammar_note: 简直: Placed before adjectives to emphasize them.
example_zh1: 你的想法简直无可挑剔。
example_en1: Your idea leaves nothing to be desired.
example_zh2: 萨米的表演简直是灾难。
example_zh3: 有些人认为阅读简直浪费时间。
example_en3: Some people think of reading as a waste of time.

grammar_note: 建立: Placed as a verb to indicate the action of setting up or establishing something.
example_zh2: 萨米建立了自己的队伍。
example_zh3: 这是建立在猜测的基础上。

grammar_note: 键盘: Used as a noun in sentences to refer to a keyboard device.
example_en1: He creates melodies on his keyboard.

grammar_note: 建设: Placed as a verb to indicate building or developing something.
example_zh2: 一座新的教学楼正在建设。
example_en2: A new school building is under construction.
example_zh3: 我需要去一趟中国建设银行。
example_en3: I need to go to the China Construction Bank.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Someone 亻 who can build 建 things; 建 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 健身: Used as a verb to express the action of keeping fit.
example_en1: Are you going to the gym today?
example_en2: I'm going to register at a gym.
example_zh3: 欣怡最近瘦好多喔，是去健身房還是失戀啊？
example_en3: Hsin-yi got so much slimmer lately. Is it gym or heartbreak?

grammar_note: 建筑: Serves as a noun referring to construction or buildings.

Translation: be particular about; to pay attention to
grammar_note: 讲究: Placed after nouns to indicate being particular about something.
example_en1: He's very sloppy in his dress.
example_zh2: 这家饭馆的餐具很讲究
example_en2: This restaurant is particular about cutlery.
example_zh3: 你看这两件做工要比那些讲究。
example_en3: See how much more carefully made these are compared to those?

grammar_note: 讲座: Serves as a noun referring to a series of lectures in a sentence.
example_zh3: 听讲座时，你应该保持安静。
example_en3: When listening to a lecture, you should be quiet.

grammar_note: 酱油: A noun representing soy sauce in a dish or statement.
example_zh1: 把米饭和鸡蛋及酱油混一下。
example_en1: Mix the rice and eggs with soy sauce.

Translation: sprinkle water on; irrigate; to water
grammar_note: 浇: Placed after subject to indicate watering an object.
交换: Placed after subjects to indicate swapping or exchanging objects.
example_zh1: 我想用汉语交换另一种语言.
example_en1: I'd like to teach you Chinese in exchange for your teaching me another language.
example_zh2: 汤姆和玛丽在长凳上交换了位置。
example_en2: Tom and Mary switched places on the bench.
example_zh3: 双方在会谈中友好地交换了看法。
example_en3: Both parties exchanged ideas cordially in the discussion.

grammar_note: 交际: Used as a noun for social interaction or communication.
example_en1: Tom knows a lot of people.
example_zh2: 我可以做中英双向翻译，参加跟外国人交际谈判。
example_en2: I can translate between Chinese and English, and can participate in negotiations with foreigners.
example_zh3: 把恋人从3D换成2D可以有效地降低交际所需的费用。
example_en3: By switching your lover from 3D to 2D, you may successfully reduce all social-interaction-related costs.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Tendons that connect 交 muscles ⺼; 交 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 胶水: A noun representing glue in a sentence as an object.

Translation: be in contact with; associate with
grammar_note: 交往: Placed after subjects to indicate interacting with others.
example_en1: We've been going out three months.
example_en2: Do you like hanging out with Tom?
example_en3: I've been going out with her for months.

grammar_note: 角度: Placed after nouns indicating perspective or viewpoint on topics.
example_en1: The angle would be too narrow.
example_zh2: 以我的角度来看，他是对的。
example_en2: The way I see it, he is right.
example_zh3: 她對任何事都用錢的角度來看。
example_en3: She thinks of everything in terms of money.

grammar_note: 狡猾: Used as an adjective to describe someone as sly or cunning.
example_zh3: 人们说，狐狸比其他动物要狡猾。
example_en3: People say that the fox is more cunning than other animals.

grammar_note: 教材: Serves as a noun referring to teaching materials in a sentence.
example_zh1: 我们有必要为上这门课买本教材吗？
example_en1: Will it be necessary for us to buy a book for this class?

grammar_note: 教练: Serves as a noun indicating a sports coach or trainer.
教训: Used as a noun to refer to a lesson learned from an experience.
example_zh2: 汤姆会被他老爸教训的。
example_en2: Tom will be scolded by his father.
example_zh3: 你必须从失败中吸取教训。

Translation: come into contact with; to get in touch with; engage
grammar_note: 接触: Placed after a subject to indicate coming into contact with something or someone.
example_zh1: 这个活塞不接触汽缸盖。
example_en1: The piston does not come into contact with the cylinder cover.
example_zh2: 我沒接触過這箇球類遊戲。
example_en2: It's a whole new ball game for me.
example_zh3: 日本有必要和西方各国接触。
example_en3: Japan needed contact with the Western countries.

grammar_note: 接待: Placed after subject to indicate receiving or admitting someone.
example_zh1: 这个家庭热情地接待了我。
example_en1: The family received me very warmly.
example_zh2: 汽车旅馆可以接待多达400名客人。
example_en2: The motel can accommodate as many as 400 guests.
example_zh3: 这次，虽然我的阅历更多但是没有人等着接待我。
example_en3: This time, although I'm more experienced, there's nobody waiting to meet me.

grammar_note: 阶段: Placed after numerals to specify a stage or phase number.
example_zh1: 今天咱们团队还有一个阶段性任务没有完成。
example_en1: There's a short-term task to be done for our team today.
example_zh2: 癌症如果在第一阶段被发现的话是很容易治愈的。
example_en2: Cancer can be cured easily if it is found in its first phase.
example_zh3: 既然所有的任务都按时完成了，我们已经准备好开始下一阶段的开发了。
example_en3: Since all tasks have been completed without delay, we are ready to start the next phase of development.

grammar_note: 接近: Placed before a noun to indicate being close to something.
example_en3: The president is difficult to approach.

grammar_note: 结实: Placed after a noun to describe it as solid or sturdy.
example_en1: This kind of cloth is both cheap and sturdy.
example_zh2: 加水，和成一个结实的面团。
example_en2: Add water and mix to a firm dough.

grammar_note: 结构: Serves as a noun indicating composition or construction in a sentence.
example_zh2: 经理打算改良公司的结构。
example_en2: The manager wants to improve the company's structuring.
example_zh3: 红树林吸取二氧化碳比地球上其他树木都要多，因为它们具有很大的地下根部结构。
example_en3: Mangroves sequester more carbon than any other trees on Earth because they have quite a large underground root structure.

grammar_note: 结合: Placed after subjects to indicate combination or integration with objects.
example_zh1: 我们可能会将你的私人信息和其他信息结合在一起。
example_en1: We may combine your personal information with other information.

grammar_note: 结论: Placed at the end of sentences to summarize or conclude.
example_zh1: 你们怎么得出这个结论的？
example_en1: How did you arrive at this conclusion?
example_zh2: 你的结论具有高度争议性。
example_zh3: 我们得出结论，这个计划目前是不可行的。
example_en3: We have come to the conclusion that this plan is not feasible currently.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 節; sections of bamboo ⺮'}
grammar_note: 节省: Placed as a verb to indicate economizing or saving resources.
example_zh1: 电脑为我们节省了很多时间，解决了很多问题。
example_en1: Computers save us a lot of time and trouble.

grammar_note: 结账: Used at the end of a service or meal to pay the bill.
example_en3: We are ready to pay the bill.

Translation: to give up or stop doing something
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Two hands 廾 brandishing a spear 戈'}
grammar_note: 戒: Placed before a verb to indicate giving up or stopping an action.
example_en1: It is difficult to give up smoking.
example_en2: It is difficult to give up smoking.

Translation: fall due; [measure word for meetings, events, etc.]
grammar_note: 届: Used as a measure word for meetings or events.
example_zh1: 在上一届世界杯上，新西兰在比赛中被墨西哥淘汰。
example_en1: In the last World Cup, New Zealand was knocked out of the competition by Mexico.

Translation: use as an excuse; on the pretext of
grammar_note: 借口: Used as a noun to refer to something used as an excuse.
example_en2: There is no use in making excuses.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Two hands 廾 brandishing a spear 戈'}
grammar_note: 戒指: A noun referring to a ring, typically used as a subject or object in sentences.
example_zh2: 他半夜給了我一枚戒指。
example_en2: He gave me a ring at midnight.
example_zh3: 我会找到你丢失的戒指。
example_en3: I will find you your lost ring.

grammar_note: 金属: Used as a noun to refer to metal in general or specific metallic substances.
example_en2: The acid ate into the metal.

grammar_note: 紧急: Used as an adjective before nouns to describe urgent situations.
example_zh1: 紧急情况下，您可以联系我。
example_en1: If there's anything urgent, you can get in touch with me.
example_zh2: 你告诉汤姆那是紧急情况了吗？
example_en2: Did Tom tell you it was an emergency?
example_zh3: 我收到汤姆的一条紧急消息。
example_en3: I have an urgent message from Tom.

grammar_note: 尽快: Placed before a verb to urge doing something as quickly as possible.
example_en2: Please come back as soon as possible.
example_en3: Please come as soon as possible.

grammar_note: 谨慎: Used as an adjective before nouns to describe being prudent or cautious.
example_en1: You must be careful in choosing your friends.
example_en3: I've been careful my whole life.

grammar_note: 进步: Placed after subject to indicate making progress.
近代: Placed before nouns to specify the period of modern times.
example_en1: The history of modern times is very interesting.
example_zh2: 近现代的建筑风格与古代大不相同。
example_en2: The architectural style of modern times is quite different from that of ancient times.
example_zh3: 他研究了中国的近代文学作品。
example_en3: He studied the works of Chinese literature from modern times.

Translation: import; entrance; sail into a port
grammar_note: 进口: Used as a verb to indicate importing goods or entering a port.
example_en1: Japan's rice market is closed to imports.
example_en2: Japan depends on other countries for oil.
example_zh3: 他想要减少进口品的税。
example_en3: He wanted to reduce the tax on imports.

Translation: to do all one can; try one's best
grammar_note: 尽力: Placed after a verb to indicate doing one's best in an action.
example_en3: I ran as fast as I could.

Translation: to the best of one's ability; as far as possible
grammar_note: 尽量: Placed before a verb to indicate doing something to the best of one's ability.
example_en2: Please speak as slowly as possible.
example_en3: I just try not to think about it.

grammar_note: 经典: Used as a noun to refer to classic works or timeless standards.
example_en1: This classic book is very valuable.
example_zh2: 我喜欢读经典文学作品。
example_en2: I like reading classic works of literature.
example_zh3: 这部电影改编自一部经典小说。
example_en3: This movie is adapted from a classic novel.

grammar_note: 精力: Placed after quantifiers or as a subject/predicate to discuss energy.
example_zh1: 我小睡后就感到精力充沛。
example_en1: A little nap and, just like that, I'm as fresh as a daisy.
example_zh2: 他不像从前那样精力充沛了。
example_en2: He isn't as energetic as he once was.
example_zh3: 他把全部精力放到实验中了。
example_en3: All his energies were devoted to the experiment.

Translation: engage in trade; be in business
grammar_note: 经商: Used as a verb to indicate engaging in business or trade activities.
example_en1: Being in business is his job.
example_en2: He decided to start doing business.
example_en3: She doesn't like engaging in trade.

grammar_note: 精神: Functions as a noun representing essence or spirit in sentences.
经营: Placed after subjects to indicate managing or operating something.
example_en1: My father has been engaged in foreign trade for many years.
example_zh2: 他的父母经营一家酒店。
example_zh3: 我们经营各种书籍，包括新的和旧的。
example_en3: We handle all type of books, both new and old.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A jar 酉 of wine 氵; 酉 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 酒吧: Serves as a noun representing a place where drinks are served.
example_en1: Mary is drinking red wine, isn't she?
example_en3: All the teachers were in the pub.

grammar_note: 救: Placed as a verb to indicate the action of rescuing or saving someone/something.
救护车: Used as a noun to refer to an ambulance in a sentence.
example_zh3: 挺住。救护车马上就来了。
example_en3: Hang on. The ambulance will get here in just a little bit.

grammar_note: 舅舅: Noun referring to one's mother’s brother.
example_en1: We are staying at our uncle's.
example_en2: My uncle is playing the guitar.
example_en3: We are spending the night at my uncle's house.

grammar_note: 居然: Placed before a verb or clause to express surprise at an outcome.
example_zh1: 我居然忘记了今天有课！
example_en1: I completely forgot that there was class today!
example_zh2: 都一天了，你居然還沒有開始！
example_en2: How come you have not started yet after a day.
example_zh3: 我没想到今天居然会哭的。
example_en3: I never expected I would end up crying today.

grammar_note: 桔子: Noun indicating a tangerine, used as an object in sentences.
example_en3: There is a tangerine on the table.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Two hands 八 writing on a tablet 目'}
grammar_note: 具备: Placed before nouns to indicate possession of qualities or abilities.
example_zh1: 孩子学钢琴要具备哪些条件？
example_en1: What are the prerequisites for a child to learn the piano?
example_zh2: 我认为，你已经完全具备了潜伏的资质。
example_en2: I believe you already possess all the qualities needed to go undercover.
example_zh3: 独立的句子和文章中的句子的区别在于后者具备上下文。
example_en3: The difference between a standalone sentence and a sentence in the middle of an essay is that the latter has context.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': "A hand holding a large carpenter's square 工"}
grammar_note: 巨大: Placed after nouns to describe their size as huge or enormous.
俱乐部: Serves as a noun representing an organization or place for shared interests.
example_en2: Do you belong to any clubs?
example_zh3: 他们选他做俱乐部主席。
example_en3: They made him the chairman of a club.

Translation: it is said; they say; allegedly
grammar_note: 据说: Placed at the beginning of a sentence to introduce reported information.
example_en1: He is said to be rich.
example_en2: It is said that Tom has a cold.
example_en3: He is said to still be in Paris.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Two hands 八 writing on a tablet 目'}
grammar_note: 具体: Placed after an adjective to specify concretely.
example_en3: The idea was brought into shape.

grammar_note: 捐: Placed after verbs to indicate donating something.
example_en2: Tom regularly donates money to charity.

grammar_note: 绝对: Placed before verbs/adjectives to emphasize absoluteness.
决赛: Placed as a noun in sentences referring to final competitions.
example_zh1: 令人遗憾的是，他并没有在决赛发挥他的最佳水平。
example_en1: The regrettable thing is that he didn't even play at his highest level in the finals.

grammar_note: 角色: Indicates a part or role in a play or society, used as a noun in sentences.
example_zh1: 你最喜欢的动漫角色是谁？
example_zh2: 胎盘的角色是滋养胎儿。
example_en2: The role of the placenta is to nourish the foetus.
example_zh3: 他扮演哈姆雷特的角色。
example_en3: He played the part of Hamlet.

grammar_note: 决心: Used as a noun to express determination or resolution in a sentence.
example_en1: He is determined to go to England.
example_en2: He made a determination to be a doctor.
example_en3: We are determined to protect the motherland.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Soldiers 冖 (distorted 力) in a cart 车'}
grammar_note: 军事: Used as a noun to refer to military affairs in a sentence.
example_zh1: 这个国家的军事力量很先进。
example_en1: The military power of this country is very advanced.

grammar_note: 均匀: Placed after nouns to describe even distribution or equality.
example_zh1: 均匀的雨滴落在大地上。
example_en1: Even raindrops fall on the ground.
example_zh3: 糖应该均匀地撒在蛋糕上。
example_en3: Sugar should be evenly sprinkled over the cake.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A card squeezed between 上 and 下'}
grammar_note: 卡车: Serves as a noun representing a lorry or truck in sentences.
example_en1: I almost got hit by a truck.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 開; hands 廾 lifting the latch 一 of a door'}
grammar_note: 开发: Placed after subjects to indicate development or exploitation actions.
example_zh1: 我正在开发一个安卓应用。
example_zh2: 为了长期利益，我们决定把开发部门卖掉。
example_en2: For the sake of long-term interests, we have decided to sell the development department.
example_zh3: 本来以为是开发板给我弄坏了，原来是电源线接触不良。
example_en3: At first I thought the development board was up the spout, but it was just a loose connection.

Translation: lift a restriction; open up (to the outside world/ public etc.)
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 開; hands 廾 lifting the latch 一 of a door'}
grammar_note: 开放: 动词，表示放宽限制或对外开放。
example_zh3: 华盛顿的樱花现在开放。
example_en3: Cherry trees are now in bloom in Washington.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 開; hands 廾 lifting the latch 一 of a door'}
grammar_note: 开幕式: Serves as a noun indicating an inauguration or opening ceremony in a sentence.
example_zh1: 我错过了奥运会的开幕式。
example_en1: I missed the opening ceremony of the Olympics.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 開; hands 廾 lifting the latch 一 of a door'}
grammar_note: 开水: Noun referring to boiling water, used directly in sentences without modifiers.
example_zh1: 阿姨，您别客气，喝杯开水就行。
example_en1: No need to trouble yourself, Auntie. A glass of boiled water will be plenty.

grammar_note: 砍: Placed as a verb to indicate cutting or chopping actions.
example_en2: A lot of trees were cut down.
example_en3: She's good at bargaining the price down.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': "Shielding one's eyes 目 with a hand 手 to look to the distance"}
grammar_note: 看不起: Placed after a subject to express disdain towards an object/person.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': "Shielding one's eyes 目 with a hand 手 to look to the distance"}
grammar_note: 看望: Placed after a subject to indicate visiting someone.
example_en1: I went there to see her.
example_en2: I came to see my father.

grammar_note: 靠: Placed after a preposition indicating action of leaning on something.

Translation: grain; [measure word for anything small and roundish]
grammar_note: 颗: Placed before nouns indicating small round objects as a measure word.

Translation: it is thus clear that; visible; visual
grammar_note: 可见: Placed at the beginning of a clause to introduce a clear conclusion.
example_en1: It is visible to the naked eye.
example_zh2: 他家后面有小溪，清可见底。
example_en2: Behind his house is a stream so clear that you can see the bottom of it.

grammar_note: 可靠: Placed after a noun to describe it as reliable or dependable.
example_en3: The report is not to be depended upon.

grammar_note: 可怕: Used as an adjective to describe something frightening or dreadful.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄'}
grammar_note: 克: Used as a measure word for small objects or abstract concepts.
课程: Serves as a noun representing a curriculum or course in a sentence.
example_zh2: 她在夜校上自卫术课程。
example_en2: She took night classes in the art of self-defense.
example_zh3: 所以你也打算选这门课程啊！
example_en3: So you're planning to follow this course as well!

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A weapon 十 used to subdue a beast 兄'}
grammar_note: 克服: Placed after subject to indicate overcoming or enduring something.
example_en2: You have to overcome the difficulties.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': "A person 各 welcomed under one's roof 宀; 各 also provides the pronunciation"}
grammar_note: 客观: Used as an adjective before nouns to describe objectivity.
example_zh2: 要小心那些说自己客观的人。
example_en2: Beware of anyone who claims objectivity.
example_zh3: 当事情发生在自己身上时，就无法客观冷静地处理。
example_en3: It's hard to stay objective and calm when it happens to you.

grammar_note: 刻苦: Used as an adjective to describe someone who is assiduous or hardworking.
example_en1: She's even more hardworking than you are.
example_en2: He's even more hardworking than you are.

grammar_note: 空间: Placed as a noun representing space or enclosed area in a sentence.
example_en1: Have you ever been to outer space?
example_zh2: 行与行之间多留些空间。
example_en2: Leave more space between the lines.

grammar_note: 空闲: Used as an adjective before nouns indicating available time.
example_zh1: 你空闲时间喜欢做什么？
example_en1: What do you like to do in your free time?
example_zh2: 您空闲时间喜欢做什么？
example_en2: What do you like to do in your free time?
example_zh3: 她利用空闲时间做布娃娃。
example_en3: She spends her leisure time making dolls.

grammar_note: 控制: Placed as a verb to indicate exercising power over something or someone.
口味: Placed after a noun to describe its taste or flavor.
example_zh2: 這個酸奶是什麼口味的？
example_en2: What flavour does this yoghurt have?
example_en3: Add salt and pepper to taste.

grammar_note: 夸: Placed after a subject to indicate boasting about something.
example_en3: I'll take that as a compliment.

grammar_note: 夸张: Used as an adjective to describe something exaggerated.
会计: Serves as a noun referring to accountancy or an accountant in sentences.
宽: Placed before nouns to describe width.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Two brothers 比 under the son 日'}
grammar_note: 昆虫: Serves as a noun referring to insects in a sentence.
example_zh3: 这种昆虫在英语中叫什么？
example_en3: What do you call this insect in English?

grammar_note: 扩大的位置在句子中作为动词，表示扩大动作。
example_zh1: 他试图扩大自己的势力范围。
example_en1: He tried to enlarge his sphere of influence.
example_zh2: 最近，来自亚洲各国的进口额不断扩大。
example_en2: The imports from Asian countries have expanded recently.

grammar_note: 辣椒: A noun representing chilli, used as a subject or object in sentences.
example_en1: Do you want pepper on it?
example_zh2: 瑪麗的包裡有辣椒噴霧。
example_en2: Mary carries pepper spray in her purse.
example_zh3: 辣椒是我最喜歡的香料之一。
example_en3: Capsicum is one of my favorite spices.

grammar_note: 拦: Placed before a verb to indicate blocking or hindering an action.
example_zh1: 警察拦下了丹的车，进行了检查。
example_en1: Police stopped Dan's car and searched it.

grammar_note: 烂: Placed after nouns to describe a state of being mashed or sodden.
example_en1: You can't raise a cat to be a dog.

Translation: read aloud; read loudly and clearly
grammar_note: 朗读: 动词，表示大声清晰地阅读。
example_en2: He reads English aloud every morning.
example_zh3: 老师让同学们朗读课文。
example_en3: The teacher asks the students to read the text aloud.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A man lifting 力 a load 冖 of grass 艹'}
grammar_note: 劳动: Used as a noun or verb to refer to work or labour.
example_en1: He is not one for hard work.
example_en2: Jim was afraid of physical labor.
example_zh3: 他对自己的劳动成果很满意。
example_en3: He was satisfied with the work he had done.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A man lifting 力 a load 冖 of grass 艹'}
grammar_note: 劳驾: Used at the beginning of a request or to seek attention politely.
example_en1: Could I have a cup of coffee?
example_en2: Could you please do me a favor?

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'A person bent over with long hair 匕 and a crutch; compare 耂'}
grammar_note: 老百姓: Used as a noun referring to common people or civilians in a sentence.
example_zh1: 許多老百姓加入了軍隊。
example_en1: A great number of citizens went into the army.
example_zh2: 自古至今，容忍的总是老百姓，被容忍的总是统治者。
example_en2: Since ancient times, it has always been the commoners who tolerate their ruler.
example_zh3: 听那些只看CCAV的老百姓进行全球经济的个人分析一直是很有趣的。
example_en3: Listening to the personal analysis about global economy made by people who watch only CCAV has always been kinda funny.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'A person bent over with long hair 匕 and a crutch; compare 耂'}
grammar_note: 老板: Used as a noun to refer to a boss or business owner.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'An older 老 woman 女; 老 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 姥姥: Noun referring to one's maternal grandmother.
example_en1: My grandma just drank a bit of soup.
example_zh2: 我在黑暗的巷子中絆倒，膝蓋砸在柏油路上。一塊木板蓋著巷弄的房屋之間的電線。深夜的巷弄非常之暗。我的眼鏡從眼睛上掉了下來。幸好有一位帶著手電筒的廣東工人幫忙。我的膝蓋只是擦破了皮。我想起另一次膝蓋摔傷是在菲律賓奎松市的唐荷西高地。那裡有一大片火星般的紅土地，遍地長滿了「塔拉希布」草。有時工人會故意縱火燒草。我和哥哥當時還在外面玩。那時我們還未到青春期。在燃燒的野草旁，我摔倒了，膝蓋著地。我的貝貝姥姥憤怒不已。家裡的女傭在車庫後面的大磁磚水槽裡幫我清洗了雙腿。
example_en2: I tripped in the alleyway in the darkness, as I crashed my knees on the asphalt. There was a wooden board that covered a wire between houses across the alleyway. It was very dark there at night. My eyeglasses fell off my face. Luckily, a Cantonese labourer with a flashlight helped me. My knees just got scraped. I remember another time when I crashed on my knees. It was at Don José Heights in Quezon City in the Philippines. There was a vastness of Martianesque red soil, wherein the "talahib" grass grew. Sometimes, workers intentionally set the grass on fire. My brother and I were still playing, even then, outside. We were still prepubescent. Near burning grass, I stumbled on my knees. My grandmother, Lola Bebe, was so angry. A maid washed my legs in the big tiled sink behind the garage.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'A person bent over with long hair 匕 and a crutch; compare 耂'}
grammar_note: 老婆: Used as a noun to refer to one's wife colloquially.
example_en3: He was afraid of his wife.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'A person bent over with long hair 匕 and a crutch; compare 耂'}
grammar_note: 老实: Used as an adjective before nouns to describe honesty or frankness.
example_en3: Not to mince words, he got fired.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'A person bent over with long hair 匕 and a crutch; compare 耂'}
grammar_note: 老鼠: Serves as a noun representing a mouse or rat in a sentence.
example_en3: There is a mouse under the table.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 樂, a musical instrument with wood 木, strings 幺, and a pick 白'}
grammar_note: 乐观: Used as an adjective to describe someone being optimistic.
example_en2: I'm sure Tom will be optimistic.
example_en3: I am not as optimistic as you are.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A storm 雨 over the fields 田'}
grammar_note: 雷: Used as a noun to denote thunder in a sentence.
example_en3: The taller the tree, the more likely it is to be struck by lightning.

grammar_note: 类型: Placed after adjectives or nouns to specify its kind or category.
example_en1: What sort of work do you do?
example_zh2: 你想看哪种类型的电影？
example_en2: What kind of movie do you want to watch?
example_zh3: 你喜欢哪种类型的音乐？
example_en3: What genres of music are you into?

Translation: treat coldly; give the cold shoulder to
grammar_note: 冷淡: Used as an adjective to describe cold treatment or attitude.
example_en1: I was very cold towards her.
example_zh2: 很多日本人對政治冷淡。
example_en2: Lots of people in Japan are indifferent to politics.
example_zh3: 據說日本人對認識的人親切，對不認識的人卻是十分冷淡。
example_en3: It is said that Japanese people are kind to people they know, but rather cold to those they don't.

grammar_note: 梨: A noun representing a pear in a sentence as a subject or object.
example_en3: This is a pear, not an apple.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'An animal standing straight; 亠 is the head'}
grammar_note: 离婚: Used as a verb to indicate the action of getting divorced.
厘米: Placed after a number to indicate centimeters.
example_zh1: 我的哥哥比我大两岁，但他却比我矮三厘米。
example_en1: My brother is two years older than I, but he is three centimeters shorter.

grammar_note: 理论: Serves as a noun representing a theory or doctrine in a sentence.
example_en1: Theory and practice should go hand in hand.
example_en2: It is difficult to understand his theory.
example_en3: I don't want to hear your theories.

grammar_note: 理由: Serves as a noun representing the reason or justification for something.
example_en1: You didn't have any reasons to be angry.
example_en2: There's no reason to get angry.
example_en3: There's no reason to be afraid.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'A man standing on the ground 一'}
grammar_note: 立即: Placed before a verb to indicate immediate action.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'A man standing on the ground 一'}
grammar_note: 立刻: Placed before a verb to indicate immediate action.
example_en3: He wants to get married right away.

grammar_note: 力量: A noun representing physical strength or power in a sentence.
利润: Placed after quantifiers or as subject/predicate in sentences discussing profit.
example_zh2: 这不过是他在谈判最后时刻尽可能最大化利润的尝试。
example_en2: It's just an attempt on his part to maximize profits, as much as possible, in the last moments of negotiations.

grammar_note: 利息: Placed after quantifiers to refer to interest rate amount.
example_en1: I have lost both principal and interest.
example_zh2: 我存在銀行的錢利息非常低。
example_en2: The money I have in the bank earns very low interest.
example_zh3: 银行对风险客户收取较高的贷款利息。
example_en3: Banks charge higher interest on loans to risky customers.

grammar_note: 利益: Placed after verbs indicating actions that yield benefits.
example_en1: Merchants only look at the profits.
example_en2: All he thinks about is himself.
example_en3: He is acting on his own behalf.

Translation: make use of; take advantage of
grammar_note: 利用: Placed before a noun to indicate using something for a purpose.
example_en1: Tom is taking advantage of you.
example_en2: I don't want to be used.
example_en3: She took advantage of my ignorance.

grammar_note: 联合: Used as a verb to indicate alliance or union between subjects.
example_zh1: 全世界无产者，联合起来！
example_zh2: 不是所有国家都加入了联合国。
example_en2: Not every country belongs to the U.N.
example_zh3: 卡尔马克思说了：“全世界无产者，联合起来！”
example_en3: Karl Marx said: "Workers of the world, unite!"

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A cart 车 moving 辶 goods between cities'}
grammar_note: 连忙: Placed before a verb to indicate doing something promptly.
example_zh2: 妈妈病了，我连忙给她送药。
example_en2: My mom is sick, I hurry to give her medicine.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A cart 车 moving 辶 goods between cities'}
grammar_note: 连续: Placed before a noun to indicate continuity.
example_zh1: 比尔连续哭了几个小时。
example_en1: Bill kept on crying for hours.
example_zh2: 他们今晚看了电视连续剧。
example_en2: They have watched TV serials this evening.
example_zh3: 小脑需要连续不断的血液供给。
example_en3: The cerebellum requires continuous blood supply.

grammar_note: 恋爱: Used as a verb indicating the act of being in love.
example_en2: No, she has never fallen in love.
example_zh3: 不，直到现在她都没有恋爱过。
example_en3: No, until now she has never fallen in love.

grammar_note: 良好: Placed after nouns as a complement to describe quality positively.
粮食: Serves as a noun representing grains or cereals in a sentence.
example_zh1: 我又转念，见日光之下，快跑的未必能赢，力战的未必得胜，智慧的未必得粮食，明哲的未必得资财，灵巧的未必得喜悦，所临到众人的，是在乎当时的机会。
example_en1: I returned, and saw under the sun, that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the strong, neither yet bread to the wise, nor yet riches to men of understanding, nor yet favor to men of skill; but time and chance happen to them all.

grammar_note: 亮: Used as an adjective before nouns to describe brightness.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'A child swaddled in blanklets; compare 子'}
grammar_note: 了不起: Used after adjectives or as a standalone term to express extraordinariness.
example_zh3: 玛丽是个了不起的女人。

grammar_note: 列车: Serves as a noun representing a train in sentences.
example_en2: The train is very crowded this evening.
example_en3: Don't get off the train till it stops.

grammar_note: 临时: Placed before nouns to indicate temporary nature.
example_en1: I'm making a last minute effort.
example_en2: A permanent job is better than a temporary one.
example_zh3: 夜幕降临时，孩子们回家了。
example_en3: The children returned home at dusk.

grammar_note: 铃: A noun representing a bell or bell-shaped objects.
灵活: Used as an adjective to describe something nimble, agile, or flexible.
example_zh2: 他是一个脑子灵活的人。

grammar_note: 零件: A noun referring to a part or component in machinery or structures.
example_zh1: 許多公司都嘗試過大規模生產這種複雜的零件，但目前只有我們成功了。
example_en1: Many companies have attempted to manufacture this complex component at scale, but so far only ours has succeeded.
example_zh2: 這台電視機是十年前製造的, 現在已經沒有零件可換, 所以要修理它是不可能的事了。
example_en2: This TV was made ten years ago and there are no parts available, so it is impossible to repair it.

grammar_note: 零食: A noun referring to snacks or small foods eaten between meals.
example_en2: I never used to eat snacks.

grammar_note: 领导: Can function as a noun (leader) or verb (to lead).
example_en1: I am the leader of this team.

grammar_note: 领域: Placed after nouns indicating a specific field or area of study/expertise.
example_en2: Is that an area you are familiar with?
example_zh3: 您专攻于中医的什么领域？
example_en3: Which aspects of Chinese medicine do you specialise in?

grammar_note: 流传: Placed after nouns to indicate spreading or circulating of ideas/things.
example_zh1: 玲奶奶死的不瞑目。流传说那栋房子至今未人敢入住。
example_en1: Grandma Ling died with unfinished business. It is said that to this day no one has dared to live in that house.
example_zh2: 这次大选创造了多项第一，也诞生了很多将世代流传的故事。但是今天晚上令我难忘的却是在亚特兰大投票的一名妇女：安-尼克松-库波尔。她和其他数百万排队等待投票的选民没有什么差别，除了一点：她已是106岁的高龄。
example_en2: This election had many firsts and many stories that will be told for generations. But one that's on my mind tonight is about a woman who cast her ballot in Atlanta. She's a lot like the millions of others who stood in line to make their voice heard in this election, except for one thing: Ann Nixon Cooper is 106 years old.

grammar_note: 浏览: Placed after it can indicate skimming or browsing through something.
流泪: Placed after subject to indicate shedding tears.
example_zh2: 如果，错过太阳的时候你在流泪，那么你也将错过群星。
example_en2: If you cry because you miss the sun when it goes away, then you will also miss the stars.

grammar_note: 龙: Used as a noun to represent a mythical creature in Chinese culture.
example_en2: The year of the dragon has ended.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Water 氵 falling like raindrops 雨; 屚 provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 漏: 动词，表示泄漏或泄露信息。
example_en2: This book is full of mistakes.

grammar_note: 陆地: Serves as a noun representing dry land or a terrace in sentences.
example_zh1: 中国陆地的总面积是960万平方公里，是亚洲面积最大的国家，居世界第三位。
example_en1: The mainland of China covers 96,000,000 square kilometers, and it is the largest country in Asia, as well as the third largest in the world.

grammar_note: 录取: Placed after subjects to indicate enrollment or admission.
example_en1: I hope to graduate at the exams.

grammar_note: 陆续: Placed before a verb to indicate actions happening in succession.
example_en2: The students came to the classroom one after another.
example_en3: Birds flew across the sky in succession.

grammar_note: 录音: Used as a verb to indicate the action of recording sound or film.
example_zh1: 这个磁带录音机不是新的。
example_en1: This tape recorder is not new.

grammar_note: 轮流: Placed after subjects to indicate taking turns.
example_en1: They'll be taking turns teaching the class.
example_en3: Tom and I took turns driving the car.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Speech 讠 that explains the logic 仑; 仑 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 论文: Serves as a noun referring to academic work like a thesis or dissertation.
example_en1: Have you finished writing your thesis?
example_en2: Are you preparing for your thesis defense?
example_en3: Your essay still needs some improvement.

grammar_note: 逻辑: Used as a noun to discuss logical reasoning or arguments.
example_en2: Do you not understand basic logic?

grammar_note: 落后: Placed after verbs to indicate falling behind or being backward.
example_zh3: 人生是一次长跑，暂时的落后和领先都不算什么。
example_en3: Life is like a marathon, where short-term gains and losses are not significant in and of themselves.

grammar_note: 骂: Placed after subject to indicate scolding or abusing someone.
example_en3: He even called me an idiot.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Simplified form of 麦; grains 來 ready to be harvested 夂'}
grammar_note: 麦克风: As a noun, it represents a microphone in a sentence.
example_en1: The probe is equipped with a microphone.

grammar_note: 馒头: A noun representing steamed bread in Chinese cuisine.
example_en1: I'll give you a mantou to eat.
example_en2: Is there a difference between steamed buns and steamed bread?
example_en3: Yesterday I bought two steamed buns.

grammar_note: 满足: Used as a verb to express satisfaction or contentment with something.
example_en1: You'll find it difficult to meet her requirements.
example_zh2: 我觉得汤姆和玛丽满足了。
example_en2: I think Tom and Mary are satisfied.
example_zh3: 罗伯特满足于现在的地位。
example_en3: Robert is content with his present position.

grammar_note: 毛病: Placed as a noun to refer to illness or fault in a sentence.
example_en2: Something is wrong with my watch.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': 'A spear pointed up and to the right'}
grammar_note: 矛盾: Used as a noun or adjective to describe contradiction or inconsistency.
example_zh2: 他们有时候有矛盾冲突
example_en2: Every now and then they clash over their differences.
example_zh3: 希望与现实之间的矛盾，因何而起？
example_en3: From what stems this contradiction between our hopes and our reality?

grammar_note: 冒险: Used as a verb to express taking risks or engaging in adventurous activities.
贸易: Serves as a noun representing trade in a sentence.
example_zh1: 最近对外贸易活动减少了。
example_en1: The activity of foreign trade has been declining of late.
example_zh2: 这两个国家有强大的贸易关系。
example_en2: The two nations have strong trade ties.
example_zh3: 日本和好几个海外国家做贸易。
example_en3: Japan trades with several foreign countries.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Picture of hair 尸 above an eye 目'}
grammar_note: 眉毛: A noun referring to eyebrows, used in specific body part references.

example_en3: Xiaolin's eyebrows are thick, his eyes are big, and his eyelashes are long.

grammar_note: 煤炭: Serves as a noun representing coal in sentences.

example_en1: Australia is the world's fifth-largest coal producer.
example_zh2: 人們很容易將能源和電力小組委員會的大多數成員描述為笨蛋。他們散佈石油和煤炭公司炮製的虛假信息，以最大限度地減少全球氣候變遷的重要性，被稱為科學文盲。
example_en2: One can easily characterize a majority of the energy and power subcommittee members as nincompoops — scientific illiterates who spread misinformation crafted by oil and coal companies in order to minimize the significance of global climate change.

grammar_note: 媒体: Serves as a noun referring to media in general.

example_en2: Concerning this issue, I feel that the trash media only report biased information.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A person 大 wearing an elegant crown 羊'}
grammar_note: 美术: Serves as a noun representing the concept of art in a sentence.

example_en3: The grandfather loves his grandchildren very much.

grammar_note: 提倡: Placed before a noun to advocate for or promote it.
example_zh2: 有没有一个国家比美国更提倡爱国主义？
example_en2: Does any other country fan the flames of patriotism as much as America?

grammar_note: 提纲: Used as a noun to refer to an outline or summary of content.
example_zh3: 我写了一份报告的提纲。
example_en3: I wrote an outline for a report.

grammar_note: 题目: Serves as a noun indicating topic, subject, or title in a sentence.
example_zh1: 这道题目没有一位老师会做。
example_en1: None of the teachers could solve the problem.
example_zh2: 即使她没生病，到了规定的日期她也完成不了她的博士论文， 因为论文题目涉及的内容太广泛。
example_en2: Even if she wasn't sick, she couldn't complete her doctoral thesis by the deadline because the thesis problem contains a vast amount of detail.

Translation: ask a question; put questions to; quiz
grammar_note: 提问: Placed after subject to indicate asking a question.
example_en2: Feel free to ask any questions.

grammar_note: 体会: 动词，表示通过经历理解或感知。
example_zh2: 我们的身体会对我们的感情做出反应。
example_en2: Our bodies respond to our feelings.

grammar_note: 体贴: Used as a verb to show consideration for others in a sentence.
example_zh3: 党为自己的利益追求势力。我们对别人不体贴；我们只追求势力。
example_en3: The Party seeks power entirely for its own sake. We are not interested in the good of others; we are interested solely in power.

grammar_note: 体现: Placed after a noun to indicate embodiment or reflection of something.
example_en1: en: 他的笑容体现了他的快乐。
example_en2: en: 这幅画体现了大自然的美好。
example_en3: en: 我们的行为应该体现我们的价值观。

grammar_note: 体验: Placed as a verb indicating the act of experiencing or learning through practice.
example_zh2: 除了雨之外，我们体验了强风。
example_en2: Besides the rain, we experienced heavy winds.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'The heavens 一 above a man 大'}
grammar_note: 天空: A noun representing the sky or heavens in a sentence.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'The heavens 一 above a man 大'}
grammar_note: 天真: Placed after nouns to describe innocence or naivety.
调皮: Used as an adjective to describe someone who is naughty or mischievous.
调整: Placed as a verb to indicate making adjustments or changes.
example_zh1: 系统会调整成允许你看到的内容。
example_en1: The system will be adjusted to what it is that you are allowed to see.
example_zh2: 由于两个竞争对手的一项新协议，我们需要重新调整战略。
example_en2: In consequence of a new agreement between two competitors, we need to readjust our strategies.

grammar_note: 挑战: Used as a verb to indicate accepting or issuing a challenge.
example_en1: Get ready to face the challenge!
example_en3: She said she enjoyed the challenge.

grammar_note: 通常: Placed before verbs to indicate usual practice or frequency.
example_en1: What time do you usually get up?

grammar_note: 统一: Used as an adjective to describe something unified or integrated.
example_en1: Is a common European identity possible?

grammar_note: 痛苦: Used as an adjective to describe pain or agony.
痛快: Used as an adjective to describe feeling very happy or satisfied.
example_zh1: 昨天我們玩得特別痛快!

grammar_note: 偷: Placed as a verb to indicate the action of stealing.
投入: Placed after verbs to indicate investment or allocation of resources.
example_zh1: 最早一批电脑1945年投入使用。
example_en1: The first electronic computers went into operation in 1945.
example_zh2: 我在这项计划上投入了所有精力。
example_en2: I've put all of my energy into this plan.
example_zh3: 該公司在這個企劃中投入了很多錢。
example_en3: The company invested a lot of money in this project.

grammar_note: 投资: Used as a verb to indicate the act of investing or as a noun for investment funds.
example_en1: How much do you have invested?
example_zh2: 她能很准确地评估投资。
example_en2: She can assess investments very accurately.
example_zh3: 谁来为风险投资提供资金？
example_en3: Who will provide capital for the venture?

grammar_note: 透明: Placed after nouns to describe transparency.
example_zh2: 你半透明的裙子让我高度兴奋。
example_en2: I am completely agog over your diaphanous dress.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A dog 犬 rushing out of a cave 穴'}
grammar_note: 突出: Placed after nouns to describe being prominent or outstanding.

Translation: territory; local god of the land
etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': "A lump of clay on a potter's wheel"}
grammar_note: 土地: Placed as a noun to refer to land or territory.
example_en1: My land abuts on the river.
example_en2: It's wasteful to leave the land lying idle.
example_zh3: 喬治被騙買了這塊土地。
example_en3: George was tricked into buying the land.

etymology: {'type': 'pictographic', 'hint': "A lump of clay on a potter's wheel"}
grammar_note: 土豆: Noun referring to potato, used as subject or object in sentences.
吐: Placed after subject to indicate vomiting or coughing up something.
兔子: As a noun, it functions as the subject or object in sentences.

Translation: dumpling; [something shaped like a ball]; [measure word for ball-like things]
etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A lot of talent 才 gathered in one place 囗'}
grammar_note: 团: Used as a measure word for round objects or in reference to dumplings.
example_en2: Have you worked the puzzle out?
example_en3: Do you take part in any community activities?

grammar_note: 推辞: Placed after verbs to decline invitations or offers.
example_zh1: 虽受邀参加今晚一个精彩万分的派对，奈何明日不得不打起精神出席会议，只好推辞了。
example_en1: I got an invitation to a party tonight that I know would be a lot of fun but I have to be in my best form for tomorrow's meeting so I had to turn it down.

grammar_note: 推广: Placed after subject to indicate spreading or popularizing something.
example_zh1: 推广新产品是公司的首要任务。
example_en1: Promoting the new product is the company's top priority.
example_zh3: 我们正在校园里推广环保意识。
example_en3: We are promoting environmental awareness on campus.

grammar_note: 推荐: Placed after verbs to suggest or recommend someone or something.
example_en2: What do you recommend to me?
example_en3: What do you recommend to me?

grammar_note: 退: Placed as a verb to indicate moving back or withdrawing.

Translation: fall behind; to do less well than before
grammar_note: 退步: 动词，表示能力或表现下降。
example_zh1: 社會不是在進步，而是在退步。
example_en1: Social conditions are going backward rather than forward.

grammar_note: 退休: Used as a verb indicating the act of retiring from work.
歪: Describes something being askew, placed after nouns to describe their state.
example_en2: A fish rots from the head down.
example_zh3: 这小女孩如果没人关心的话，就要走上歪路了。
example_en3: The little girl will go astray if no one cares much about her.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Night-time 夕 divinations 卜; the supernatural, the foreign'}
grammar_note: 外公: A noun referring to one's paternal grandfather.
example_zh2: 我们担心着外公和外婆。
example_en2: We're worried about Grandma and Grandpa.
example_zh3: 我妈妈的爸爸是我的外公。
example_en3: My mother's father is my maternal grandfather.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Night-time 夕 divinations 卜; the supernatural, the foreign'}
grammar_note: 外交: Placed after verbs related to state functions indicating diplomatic actions or affairs.
example_zh3: 必须有外交解决的途径。
example_en3: There must be a way to arrive at a diplomatic solution.

grammar_note: 玩具: A noun referring to toys, used as the subject or object in sentences.
example_en3: The boy is playing with his toy soldiers.

grammar_note: 完美: Used as an adjective to describe something as perfect or flawless.
完善: Used as a verb to indicate improving and perfecting something or an adjective for perfection.
example_zh1: 这个系统存在着许多缺陷和不尽完善的地方。
example_en1: This system is bristling with defects and drawbacks.
example_zh2: 一些大学生在假期去非洲做志愿者 ，帮助当地完善野生生物管理。
example_en2: During the holidays, some university students go to Africa as volunteers and help to perfect local wildlife conservation.

grammar_note: 完整: Used as an adjective to describe completeness or wholeness of something.
example_en2: Did you read the whole book?

Translation: just in case; if by any chance
grammar_note: 万一: Placed at the beginning of a clause to express contingency.
example_zh1: 万一你生病了，吃这个药。
example_en1: Take this medicine in case you get sick.
example_zh2: 万一我来晚的话，就别等我了。
example_en2: Should I be late, don't wait for me.
example_zh3: 万一来不了，我会先给你打电话。
example_en3: In case I can't come, I'll give you a call beforehand.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A man 十 bridging heaven and earth (both 一)'}
grammar_note: 王子: Noun referring to a prince or king's son in a sentence.
example_en1: The prince succeeded to the throne.
example_en3: The prince was lost in the woods.

Translation: go there and back; come and go
grammar_note: 往返: Used as a verb phrase indicating round trips or reciprocal movements.
网络: Serves as a noun referring to internet or network in sentences.
example_zh3: 我在下载这份网络档案。

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A person 㔾 at the edge of a cliff 厃; 厃 also provides the pronunciation'}
grammar_note: 危害: Placed after verbs to indicate causing harm or damage.
example_zh1: 奴役制是一种危害人类罪。
example_en1: Slavery is a crime against humanity.
example_zh2: 有些药品会对身体产生危害。
example_en2: Some medicines can be harmful to the body.
example_zh3: 吸烟真是又恶心又低俗！点根烟然后吸，把这些危害健康的气体吸进肺里，然后呼出肮脏的气味。
example_en3: What a disgusting and stupid vice smoking is! Lighting a cigarette and sucking in the smoke. Breathing a dangerous threat to your health into your lungs. Exhaling a foul odor.

grammar_note: 微笑: A noun referring to a gentle smile, used as a subject or object in sentences.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'Dominating a woman 女 by force of arms 戈'}
grammar_note: 威胁: Placed as a verb to indicate threatening or menacing someone or something.
example_en1: He threatened to make it public.
example_en3: I am not in the least afraid of his threats.

grammar_note: 违反: Placed before nouns to indicate violation of rules/laws.
example_zh2: 汤姆一向违反知识产权。
example_zh3: 汤姆不知道他的所作所为违反了规则。
example_en3: Tom didn't know that what he'd done was against the rules.

grammar_note: 围巾: A noun representing a scarf, muffler, or neckerchief in a sentence.
example_en1: Why are you wearing that scarf?
example_zh2: Vanessa喜欢针织彩虹色的帽子、围巾和连指手套。
example_en2: Vanessa loves to knit hats, scarves, and mittens in rainbow colors.
example_zh3: 我想给妻子买一件礼物。我打算买一条围巾。
example_en3: I would like to buy a present for my wife. I thought about a scarf.

grammar_note: 围绕: Placed before a noun to indicate focusing on or revolving around it.
example_zh1: 那里有许多雏菊围绕着钢铁大厦。
example_en1: There are daisies around the steel building.
example_zh2: 这个词后来被用来指代围绕大天体的小天体。
example_en2: The word came to be used for all small heavenly bodies revolving about larger ones.

Translation: keep in good repair; service; maintain
grammar_note: 维修: Used as a verb to indicate maintenance or repair of something.
example_zh2: 家里需要维修的地方很多。
example_en2: There are many places in the house that need repairs.

grammar_note: 唯一: Placed before a noun to indicate it is the only one of its kind.
example_en1: This is the only way in.
example_en2: It was the only way to go.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A furry 毛 tail behind a body 尸'}
grammar_note: 尾巴: A noun placed after descriptors to refer to an appendage or tail.
example_en1: The dog was wagging his tail.
example_en3: The dog followed its owner, wagging its tail.

grammar_note: 伟大: Used as an adjective to describe greatness or magnitude.
example_en1: Great is the power of habit.
example_en3: Great thoughts are created through intricate details.

grammar_note: 委屈: Used as a verb to express feeling wronged or as an adjective to describe being treated unfairly.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'The stomach ⺼ behind the abdominal muscles 田'}
grammar_note: 胃: A noun representing the stomach in anatomical contexts.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A wheat plant that has not yet borne fruit; compare 來'}
grammar_note: 未必: Placed before a verb to express possibility or uncertainty.
example_en3: This work is not necessarily easy.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'The stomach ⺼ behind the abdominal muscles 田'}
grammar_note: 胃口: Placed after quantifiers or before verbs related to eating.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'A wheat plant that has not yet borne fruit; compare 來'}
grammar_note: 未来: Placed before nouns to indicate the future aspect.

etymology: {'type': 'ideographic', 'hint': 'The place where a person 亻 stands 立'}
grammar_note: 位于: Placed before a location to indicate where something is situated.
example_en2: The church is at the foot of a mountain.
example_en3: The library is in the middle of the city.
